January 25, 1940.    Morning Translation.

Ta Mei Pao, Sin Wan Pao, Shun Pao, National Herald, Hwa Pao,
Chinese-American Daily News :-

PEOPLE'S FOOD READJUSTMENT ASSOCIATION ADDRESSES
OPEN LETTER TO LOCAL RESIDENTS.

The Shanghai People's Food Readjustment
Association on January 24 issued an open letter addressed
to local residents containing the following five points :-
(1) For certain reasons, there is a possibility for a
further increase in the price of rice in Shanghai.
It is to be hoped that people in various walks of life
will purchase large quantities of rice as soon as
possible so that fears of a shortage may not arise
again in future.
(2) Factories, stores, schools and other public bodies and
organizations should advance money to their employees
for the purchase of rice that may be kept for over
six months (Saigon rice can be kept in good condition
for two years) and the money thus advanced may be
deducted from the wages of the employees. This will
not cause much loss to the managements, but it will
calm the minds of their employees at their work.
Two-thirds of the population in Shanghai are workers.
If they are saved all worry over food supplies for a
period of six months, the question of food supplies for
the whole of Shanghai will be settled.
(3) The Association approved that people in various walks
of life collect the money and place joint orders for
rice from abroad. People should refrain from purchasing
large quantities of rice in Shanghai for this will
reduce stocks in this locality, thereby seriously
affecting the livelihood of poor people.
(4) People should realize the gravity of the question of
food supplies for the future and adopt measures for the
joint purchase of rice.
(5) The following questions and answers are published to
enable the people to understand the meaning of the
joint purchase of rice :-
Q: Why is it necessary to order foreign rice?
A: For certain reasons, the sources of supplies of
Chinese rice cannot be depended upon. Therefore it
is necessary to order foreign rice.
Q: What is the price of foreign rice per "zar"?
A: The Association has ordered two lots of Saigon rice.
The first order is for 6,000 bags at $43.83 and the
second order is for 10,000 bags at $48.83. Roughly,
one bag of rice weighs one "zar" and a quarter.
Q: According to present conditions, is the price of
foreign rice cheap?
A: The rice stocks in Shanghai are limited and trouble
will arise as soon as these stocks are sold. So,
local people should lose no time in purchasing foreign
rice as a precaution against trouble.
Q: Does the People's Food Readjustment Association
collect any fees from people ordering rice?

人民食粮调整协会致
本地居民的公开信。

上海人民食粮调整协会于1月24日发布了一封致本地居民的公开信，包含以下五点：-
(1) 出于某些原因，上海米价有可能进一步上涨。
希望各界人士尽快大量购买大米，以免将来再次出现对短缺的恐慌。
(2) 工厂、商店、学校及其他公共机构和组织应预支资金给员工，用于购买可储存六个月以上的大米（西贡米可保持良好状态两年），预支款项可从员工工资中扣除。这对管理层不会造成太大损失，但能安抚员工在工作时的焦虑情绪。
上海人口中有三分之二是工人。如果他们能在六个月内免除对粮食供应的所有担忧，整个上海的粮食供应问题就将得到解决。
(3) 协会赞同各界人士集资并向国外联合订购大米。人们应避免在上海大量购买大米，因为这将减少本地库存，从而严重影响穷人的生计。
(4) 人们应认识到未来粮食供应问题的严重性，并采取联合购米的措施。
(5) 发布以下问答，以便民众理解联合购米的含义：-
问：为何有必要订购外国大米？
答：出于某些原因，中国大米的供应来源不可依赖。因此有必要订购外国大米。
问：外国大米每“扎尔”（zar）的价格是多少？
答：协会已订购两批西贡米。第一批订单为6,000袋，单价43.83元；第二批订单为10,000袋，单价48.83元。大致上，一袋大米重一“扎尔”又四分之一。
问：根据目前情况，外国大米价格便宜吗？
答：上海的大米库存有限，一旦这些库存售罄，麻烦就会出现。因此，本地居民应不失时机地购买外国大米，以防患于未然。
问：人民食粮调整协会是否向订购大米的人收取任何费用？

page_data.en:
January 25, 1940. Morning Translation.

A: Not a single cash is collected. The Association
is working for the people free of charge. The
accounts are open to the public and the rice ordered
is distributed among people at the original price.
Members and employees of the Association draw no pay.
Two or three paid clerks have been engaged. The
Association can carry on for several months and there
is no need to ask financial assistance from the public.
A sum of $1,500 has been contributed by members of the
Association.
Q: Why does the People's Food Readjustment Association
desire to collect funds?
A: The Association must have a certain amount of funds
on hand in order to attain its object of improving
the rice situation. For instance, when the price
of rice is low, it may buy rice with the funds, and
when the price goes up, it sells the rice. This
may stabilize the rice price. If the quantities of
rice ordered by the public are not large and should
the price register a drop at this time and the foreign
exchange rate improves, the Association may purchase
rice if it is in possession of funds.
All this shows the importance of having funds
on hand. The public should raise funds for the
Association. The money will be repaid according to
the regulations.

问：未收取分文。本会为民服务，不取报酬。账目公开，所订购之大米按原价分发给民众。本会会员及职员均不支薪。仅雇佣了两三名带薪办事员。本会可维持数月运作，无需向公众寻求财政援助。本会会员已捐款1,500元。
答：人民食米调剂协会为何希望募集资金？
问：本会必须手头拥有一定数额的资金，以实现改善米荒状况的目标。例如，当米价低廉时，可用资金购米；待米价上涨时，再将米售出。此举可稳定米价。若公众订购的大米数量不多，且此时米价下跌、外汇汇率好转，若本会持有资金，便可购入大米。
这一切都表明手头拥有资金的重要性。公众应为本会募集资金。款项将按规定偿还。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. B. REGISTRY
No. S. B. D.

Three Piculs of Rice
Stolen by Mob

Wheelbarrows Attacked by
40 Chinese ; Two Arrested

Yet another minor rice riot was
reported yesterday afternoon, when a
mob of about 40 male and female
Chinese attacked several wheelbar-
rows with rice and stole about three
piculs of the valuable cereal. An
alarm raised by the coolies attracted
the attention of policemen and re-
sulted in the arrest of two persons,
a man and a woman, who will face
the First Special District Court this
morning.
According to investigations conduct-
ed by detectives from Central station,
several wheelbarrows of rice were
despatched to a Chinese restaurant
at 47 Shantung Rd. While proceeding
along Foochow Road, just a few yards
from Shantung Road, the caravan of
wheelbarrows was attacked by the
mob.
The leader, it was learned, was
armed with a safety razor blade and
with this instrument he cut three
bags. Rice poured out and Chinese
fought to get some of it, filling their
pockets, pieces of cloth and baskets
with the cereal.
The attacked wheelbarrow coolie
immediately shouted for help and his
call was answered by policemen, who
rushed to the scene. Seeing the ap-
proach of constables, the mob scat-
tered, some making their getaway by
running into alleyways in the vicin-
ity, others along Foochow Road and
intersecting streets. The policemen
were, however, able to arrest the
ringleader and the woman. The
former was found in possession of
the safety razor blade.
Taken to the station, they confessed
to having participated in the attack,
blaming the very high cost of rice
for their crime.

三担大米
遭暴民抢劫

四十名华人袭击独轮车；两人被捕

昨日下午又发生一起小型米骚乱，据报约四十名男女华人袭击了几辆装载大米的独轮车，抢走了约三担这种珍贵的谷物。苦力发出的警报引起了警察的注意，导致一男一女两人被捕，他们将于今晨在第一特区法院受审。
根据中央捕房侦探进行的调查，几辆装有大米的独轮车被派往山东路47号的一家华馆。当车队沿福州路行进，距山东路仅数码之遥时，遭到暴民袭击。
据悉，带头者手持一枚安全刀片，并用此工具割破了三个米袋。大米倾泻而出，华人们争相抢夺，将谷物装满口袋、布片和篮子。
受袭的独轮车苦力立即呼救，警察闻声赶来。看到巡捕 approaching（逼近），暴民四散奔逃，有的跑进附近的小巷，有的沿福州路及相交街道逃窜。然而，警察成功逮捕了头目和那名女子。前者被发现持有安全刀片。
带到捕房后，他们承认参与了袭击，并将罪行归咎于高昂的米价。

Rice Cargo
Stormed By
Hungry Mob

Two Arrested With Razor
Blade Used In Cutting
Open Bags Of Rice

Demonstrating the effects of the
worsening rice situation upon the
lower crust of the Chinese populace
here, three wheelbarrows laden
with rice were mobbed yesterday
afternoon by a crowd of 40 hungry
people just within the shadow of the
Headquarters of the Shanghai
Municipal Police, on Foochow Road.
One male and one female Chinese
were subsequently arrested and one
razor blade used in cutting the bags
of rice open was seized by officers
from Central Station.
Investigation conducted by
detectives on the case revealed that
at about 2.30 p.m. yesterday, a large
quantity of rice was being conveyed
in three wheelbarrows to a Chinese
restaurant at 47 Shantung Road.
As the cargo reached a spot on
Foochow Road, near Shantung
Road, about 40 men and women, a
typical conglomeration of beggars
and waifs who live in the streets,
stormed the wheelbarrows.
One of them was observed to
have produced a sharp razor blade
and quickly cut openings in three
of the bags, whereupon each and
everyone of the mob helped himself
to the indispensable cereal. Helpless
in the face of imminent violence,
the coolies pushing the wheelbar-
rows dashed to Central Station,
only half a block away, and report-
ed the riot.
A party of detectives and
uniformed men subsequently rushed
to the spot and scattered the
marauders, arresting one male and
one female who will be accordingly
charged in the First Special Dis-
trict Court at 10 a.m. today. The
razor blade will be presented as an
exhibit.

运米货物
遭饥饿暴民冲击

两人因使用刀片割开
米袋而被捕

此事显示了日益恶化的米荒状况对上海底层华人民众的影响，昨日下午，在福州路上海公共租界工部局警务处总部阴影笼罩之下，三辆装载大米的独轮车遭到一群40名饥饿民众的围攻。
随后一名华籍男子和一名华籍女子被捕，中央捕房警官缴获了一把用于割开米袋的剃须刀片。
侦探对此案的调查显示，昨日下午约2时30分，大量大米正由三辆独轮车运往山东路47号的一家华馆。
当货物到达福州路靠近山东路的一处地点时，约40名男女——典型的由生活在街头的乞丐和流浪儿组成的混杂人群——冲击了独轮车。
有人观察到其中一人掏出一把锋利的剃须刀片，迅速割开了三个米袋，随即暴民中的每个人都自行取用这种不可或缺的谷物。面对迫在眉睫的暴力束手无策，推独轮车的苦力冲向仅半条街区之遥的中央捕房报案。
随后，一队侦探和制服警员赶赴现场，驱散了劫掠者，逮捕了一男一女，他们将于今日上午10时在第一特区法院被起诉。该剃须刀片将作为证物呈堂。

page_data.en:
At 2.10p.m. 3/11/40, Informant Kung Yung O
(龔永祺), Senior assistant of a rice shop
located at 1954 Bubbling Well Road, reported to
the station that at about 1.50 p.m. even date,
his apprentice Kao Chia Wah (高家華) age 15,
was held up by some 20 female Chinese on Sinsa
Road near Hart Road and relieved him of 4 sacks
of rice value $120.00.

Inquiries by detectives revealed that the
apprentice was told to deliver 4 sacks of rice
to a customer on Gordon Road. The rice was
loaded on a hand trolley and whilst he was
proceeding along Sinsa Road with the handtrolley,
several female Chinese came from Hart Road and
stopped him. Two of them then held him up
while the remainder, some 20 in number, cut open
the sacks with small pocket knives which they
were carrying and stole the contents. The two
females released their hold when all the rice
had been taken away by their accomplices.
All the females were seen carrying away the rice
with bags or tin containers and it appears that
they are a gang of organised rice thieves.

The victim did not raise an alarm and he
returned to his shop after being robbed. Scene
of offence is located on North of Sinsa Road near
Hart Road. Nearest policemen in the vicinity at
the time were C.P.C.s 2748 and 2749, they were
at Sinsa Road extension, approximately 100 yards
away from the scene.
page_data.zh:
1940年11月3日下午2:10，报案人 Kung Yung O (龔永祺)，静安寺路1954号一家米店的高级店员，向捕房报告称，同日约下午1:50，其学徒 Kao Chia Wah (高家華)，15岁，在新闸路近哈同路处被约20名华籍女性拦劫，抢走4袋大米，价值120.00美元。

侦探的调查揭示，该学徒奉命将4袋大米送给戈登路的一位顾客。大米装在手推车上，当他推着手推车沿新闸路行进时，几名华籍女性从哈同路出来拦住他。其中两人将其按住，其余约20人则用随身携带的小折叠刀割开米袋，偷走内容物。当所有大米被同伙拿走后，这两名女性才松手。
所有女性都被看到用袋子或锡罐将大米带走，看来她们是一个有组织的大米盗窃团伙。

受害人未发出警报，被抢后返回店内。案发地点位于新闸路北段近哈同路处。当时附近最近的警察是华籍巡捕 2748号和2749号，他们位于新闸路延伸段，距案发现场约100码。

At 10.45a.m. 25/9/40, C.P.C. 1636 accompanied
by informants Tien Ching Kung (錢金根), and Kyi
Zai Ching (季瑞清, both coolies employed by one
named Zah Mei Shing (柴梅興, residing Klangwan,
brought to the station the two accused for being
concerned in the theft of three sacks of rice, valued
$200.00.

Enquiries made by D.S. Weeks and C.D.C. 338
revealed that, at 10a.m. 25/9/40, whilst the coolies
were pulling a wheelbarrow loaded with rice, on
Avenue Road near Ferry Road, about 100 male and
female Chinese attacked the coolies and stole three
sacks of rice.

The coolies succeeded in effecting the arrest
of the two accused, whilst the remainder escaped.

Tien Ching Kung (錢金根 was stabbed on the
right leg during the scuffle and was sent to the Red
Cross Hospital. Dr's certificate states: "Cutting
wound of right leg."

Both accused denied being concerned in the
offence, but were unable to explain why they were
in possession of a quantity of rice, valued $1.00.

They have been charged accordingly and will
appear before the S.S.D. Court on the 26/9/40 for
trial.

1940年9月25日上午10时45分，巡捕房警长（C.P.C.）1636号在线人钱金根（Tien Ching Kung）和季瑞清（Kyi Zai Ching，音译）的陪同下，将两名被告带至警局，二人涉嫌盗窃三袋大米，价值200.00美元。上述线人均为柴梅興（Zah Mei Shing，音译，住康乐里/Klangwan）雇用的苦力。

经警司（D.S.）Weeks和刑事侦缉处警员（C.D.C.）338号调查查明，1940年9月25日上午10时，当这些苦力在爱文义路（Avenue Road）靠近斐伦路（Ferry Road）处拉着一辆装载大米的独轮车时，约有100名中国男女袭击了苦力并抢走了三袋大米。

苦力们成功逮捕了两名被告，其余人逃脱。

钱金根在扭打过程中右腿被刺伤，已被送往红十字会医院。医生证明书写道：“右腿切割伤。”

两名被告均否认参与该罪行，但无法解释为何持有价值1.00美元的大米。

据此已对他们提出指控，他们将于1940年9月26日出庭受审，由上海特区地方法院（S.S.D. Court）审理。

“B”区副督察长（Sen. D.D.O. "B"）。

THEFT OF RICE ON GORDON ROAD

At 7 a.m. yesterday, a case of theft of rice occurred at the corner of Gordon and Avenue Roads. Some 30 or 40 poor women and children who had gathered on the streets, each carrying tin buckets etc., stole a quantity of rice from a wheelbarrow laden with rice. Seeing this, the wheelbarrow coolie cried for help and assaulted the women and children with a cloth belt which he uses in pushing the vehicle. Notwithstanding this, the crowd became larger and it was impossible for the coolie to stop them. When post duty policemen reached the scene, over half of the four "zar" of rice on the vehicle had been removed.

1946年7月12日 上午
《新闻报》-

戈登路大米盗窃案

昨天上午7时，戈登路（Gordon Road）和爱文义路（Avenue Road）拐角处发生了一起大米盗窃案。约三四十名聚集在街头的贫困妇女儿童，每人携带铁桶等物，从一辆装满大米的独轮车上偷走了一定数量的大米。独轮车苦力见此情景大声呼救，并用推车时使用的布带殴打这些妇女儿童。尽管如此，人群越来越多，苦力无法阻止他们。当值班警察到达现场时，车上的四“扎”大米中已有超过一半被搬走。

REPORT

Subject Press Report - Women snatch rice from hand trolley on Markham Road.

Made by and Forwarded by D. I. Crawford.

With reference to the attached translation
from Chinese newspapers dated June 30, 1940, on the
above subject, enquiries ascertained that at 10 a.m.
June 29, when a coolie named Kyung Kiang Sing
(冀江新) of the Nanchang Rice Shop, 301 Sinza Road,
was delivering three bags of rice by means of a
handtrolley near the Markham Road Bridge, some 40
poor people of the begger class mostly women and
children surrounded him. They cut the bags with knives
and scooped up the rice escaping. The coolie reported
the matter to a policeman in the vicinity who
succeeded in arresting two of the crowd, namely :-
Li Soo Sz (李蘇氏), age 40, native of Shantung,
residing in straw hut on Penang Road.
Wu Zi Sz (吴齊氏), age 31, native of Kompo,
residing in Chapei.
They were taken to Sinza Station and were arraigned
before the Shanghai Special District Court on the
morning of July 2 and each sentenced to 4 months'
imprisonment suspended for two years (Sinza F.I.R.
1993/40).

$30 worth of rice was stolen it was estimated.

C. Crawford

关于附件中1940年6月30日中文报纸关于上述主题的译文，经查证，1940年6月29日上午10时，新闸路301号南昌米店的一名名为冀江新（Kyung Kiang Sing，音译）的苦力，用手推车运送三袋大米经过马格纳路（Markham Road）桥附近时，被约40名乞丐阶层的穷人（多为妇女和儿童）包围。他们用刀割开袋子，舀起大米后逃逸。该苦力向附近的一名警察报案，警察成功逮捕了人群中的两人，即：

June 30, 1940. Morning Translation.

National Herald, Ta Mei Pao, Chinese-American Daily News,
Sin Wan Pao:

WOMEN SNATCH RICE FROM HAND TROLLEY ON MARKHAM ROAD

At about 10 a.m. yesterday whilst passing by
one end of the Markham Road Bridge, a hand trolley laden
with three bags of rice was halted by a group of poor
Kompo women who dashed out from the roadside and dispersed
after they had snatched several tens of catties of rice
from the bags.
The coolie immediately made a report to a
policeman on post duty who gave chase and effected the
arrest of two women. The arrested women were taken to
the Police Station to be dealt with.

With reference to the attached letter
purporting to have emanated from the "Settlement
and French Concession Citizens' Association for
Dealing with Unscrupulous Merchants" (上海公共租界市民聯合整奸團) which was received by the Shanghai
Municipal Council on June 24, 1940, discreet
enquiries have failed to ascertain any particulars
of such an organization.

An examination of the letter shows that
the letter was posted at the General Post Office,
North Szechuen Road, at 11 p.m. June 21, 1940,
and is written on two sheets of ruled paper torn
from an exercise book. The envelope is an ordinary
Chinese style one.

Mr. May Yoh (梅堉), Clerical Assistant,
Crime Branch Headquarters, perused the composition
and writing but found no similarity with letters
in his office.

It is considered from the composition that
the letter is the work of one individual who
allows a feeling to run through the letter and
is hard hit by the recent high price of rice. If
the letter was written by an organized party, it
is thought that the letter would have been written
on letter head paper or paper of better quality.

ice prices : Threat of disturbance.
Since the beginning of this year the prices of all
commodities, especially foodstuffs, have rapidly risen. Though
Price Control Committees have been formed, we regret that they
have only the power to operate petty dealers. No attention is
given to the very insistent demands from residents to force
down the prices of foodstuffs, and no suitable step has been
taken to bring this about. The price of rice has now risen
to more than 70 per picul. How can the poor people, who buy
our rice from day to day, continue to exist? Not only do we
find it difficult to eke out a day's existence as to pass a
whole year, but to provide for food for a meal is an equally
difficult problem. Our hardships cannot be fully described.
The members of the Price Control Committees seem not to be
doing their duties properly. Have they achieved any success
in forcing down prices?

Driven by hunger, we are now compelled to take desperate
action. We have formed ourselves into a body whose sole object
is to deprive the various unscrupulous merchants of all their
stocks of foodstuffs stored in different godowns or junks and
private godowns. Our slogan is: "When there is any rice, it
shall be shared by all; when the rice is exhausted, the hardship
must be borne equally by all".

Fortunately our organization is receiving the support of
citizens, and a large number of persons have joined us.

米价：骚乱威胁。
今年以来，所有商品，尤其是食品的价格迅速上涨。虽然
已成立物价管制委员会，但遗憾的是，它们只有权管理小商贩。对于居民要求压低食品价格的迫切呼声，未予重视，也未采取适当措施予以解决。目前米价已涨至每担70元以上。每日买米度日的贫民如何生存？不仅难以维持一年的生计，就连解决一顿饭食也成了同样困难的问题。我们的苦难无法尽述。
物价管制委员会的成员似乎未能妥善履行职责。他们在压低价格方面取得了任何成效吗？

在饥饿的驱使下，我们现在被迫采取孤注一掷的行动。我们已组成一个团体，其唯一目标是剥夺各不法商人在不同仓库、驳船及私人仓库中储存的所有食品库存。我们的口号是：“有米同享，米尽同难”。

幸运的是，我们的组织正得到市民的支持，已有大量人员加入。

page_data.en:
- 2 -

the last few days our membership enrolment has been grown to
1,595 persons. I presume that you will be greatly surprised
by this statement and will probably not believe it.
We have been proceeding smoothly and quickly about this
business; we need only some hundred permanent members to
hire us the people who, whether with smiling faces or angry
looks, will in large bodies at once join the ranks. Our orders
will be carried out with lightning speed, and although our
members are scattered over wide areas, and engaged in various
vocations, they will respond to our call within a few hours.
The rules of the association are given as follows:
Name: The Anti-Cost of Living and Conscientious Citizens'
Association for Dealing with Unscrupulous Merchants
Object: To commandeer hoardings of unscrupulous dealers in
foodstuffs.
Number of members: 30,000 persons.
Organization: Members are organized on a military footing.
They will form one regiment consisting of 3 battalions, each
battalion consisting of 3 companies, each company consisting of
3 sub-companies, each sub-company consisting of 3 platoons, each
platoon consisting of 3 sub-platoons, and each sub-platoon
consisting of 40 members, plus 24 pickets and 8 reserve members.
We shall have a staff headquarters, accounts office and intelligence
corps.
With such a well organized body of men we shall be able to
cope with any situation, and to match ourselves with the combined
strength of policemen, and detectives who serve as catapaws for
profiteers.
Gentlemen. Why we address this letter to you, is firstly,
because we wish to beg you to take immediate steps to reduce the
prices of commodities, and secondly, because we wish to notify
and warn you in advance. Should you continue to act in your own
interest and take no measures to lower prices and relieve the distress
of the poor, we shall be driven to desperate acts, though our

在过去几天里，我们的会员人数已增至
1,595人。我想这一陈述会使你们大为惊讶，并且可能不相信。
我们在此事上的进展顺利且迅速；我们只需几百名永久成员来雇佣那些无论面带笑容还是怒容满面的人，他们将大批立即加入我们的行列。我们的命令将以闪电般的速度执行，尽管我们的成员分散在广阔区域，从事各种职业，但他们将在几小时内响应我们的号召。
本会章程如下：
名称：反生活费用高昂及良心市民联合整奸团
目标：征用不法食品商人的囤积物资。
会员人数：30,000人。
组织：会员按军事编制组织。他们将组成一个团，下辖3个营，每个营下辖3个连，每个连下辖3个排，每个排下辖3个班，每个班由40名成员组成，外加24名哨兵和8名后备成员。我们将设有参谋总部、会计室和情报科。
拥有如此组织严密的队伍，我们将能够应对任何局势，并与作为奸商爪牙的警察和侦探的联合力量相抗衡。
诸位先生。我们致信给你们，首先是因为我们希望恳请你们立即采取措施降低商品价格，其次是因为我们希望提前通知并警告你们。如果你们继续只顾自身利益，不采取措施降低价格并缓解贫民的困苦，我们将被迫采取孤注一掷的行动，尽管我们的

page_data.en:
- 3 -

lives may be forfeited or we be imprisoned. As our regiment
is brave, there is no doubt but that we shall achieve our object.
Being hungry we cannot do otherwise than act. There is nothing
that we fear. What do we care for law when we are starving
to death? We will not commit murder or arson; we are hungry
and compelled to risk our lives. This is only the natural
result of the doings of those hard-hearted and unscrupulous
dealers who commit bloodless murder. We are driven to this
dangerous pass, and fear nothing. We have committed no crime;
but we want the blood of those unscrupulous dealers who commit
bloodless murders. We think perhaps you may even approve
our actions, sympathize with us and pardon us. Please wait
and see. Please watch for the outbreak.

(Signed) Shanghai Settlement and French
Concession Citizens' Association for
dealing with unscrupulous merchants.

(Note: Received for translation late a.m. 24th June, 1940).

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL TRANSLATION OFFICE JUN 24 1940）

- 3 -

生命可能会丧失或我们会被监禁。由于我们的团英勇无畏，毫无疑问我们将实现我们的目标。
因为饥饿，我们不得不行动。我们无所畏惧。当我们饿死时，谁还在乎法律？我们不会犯谋杀或纵火罪；我们只是饥饿所迫，不得不冒生命危险。这只是那些心狠手辣、进行无形谋杀的不法商人行径的自然结果。我们被逼入此险境，无所畏惧。我们没有犯罪；但我们想要那些进行无形谋杀的不法商人的血。我们认为你们甚至可能会赞同我们的行动，同情我们并宽恕我们。请拭目以待。请注视事态的爆发。

（签名）上海公共租界及法租界
市民联合整奸团。

At 8.25 p.m. on 21-6-40, a telephone message
was received by Wayside Station to the effect that a
crowd of Chinese were looting rice on East Yuhang Road
near Kungping Road.

A party of Police followed up by members of the
Japanese Naval Landing Party attended and dispersed
a mob of about 300 persons who were looting rice from a
newly opened rice shop located at 934 East Yuhang Road.

At the conclusion of the clash, C.D.S. 305 and
the undersigned observed the accused:-

Tseu Nyi Dau (周二道), 33, Ningpo, S-Hawker,
20 Ching Sing Li, East Yuhang Road.

leap over the counter from the aforementioned shop
into the roadway where following a chase, his arrest
was effected..

Questioned by detectives the accused admits
that he with other unknown male Chinese entered the
shop and stole rice.

In view of the admission of the above named
coupled with the fact that -- according to the complt.
14 bags of rice value $400.00 were stolen, the
accused will be arraigned before the S. S. D. Court
to answer a charge of Larceny Cont. to Art. 320 (1)
of the C.C.R.C.

1940年6月21日晚上8:25，韦赛德警察局接到电话消息，称有一群中国人在公平路附近的东余杭路抢劫大米。

一队警察随后在日本海军陆战队成员的支援下赶到，驱散了约300名正在东余杭路934号一家新开业米店抢劫大米的暴徒。

冲突结束时，刑事侦缉处第305号和下述警官观察到被告：

周二道（Tseu Nyi Dau），33岁，宁波人，小贩，东余杭路庆生里20号。

从上述商店跳过柜台进入马路，经过追捕后将其逮捕。

经侦探讯问，被告承认他与其他不知名的中国男子进入商店并偷窃大米。

鉴于上述供认，加之据投诉人称——14袋价值400.00美元的大米被盗，被告将被提解至特区地方法院，以回答违反《中华民国刑法》第320条第(1)款的盗窃罪指控。

At 10.52 a.m. 23/2/40 a telephone message was
received from the Yuen Foong (阮丰) Rice Shop,
No.106-8 Linching Road, to the effect that an
unsuccessful attempt had been made to steal a sack
of rice from the shop by two Kompo coolies who had
made good their escape.

Enquiries however, ascertained the following.

At about 10.40 a.m. 23/2/40 two male Chinese
of the coolie class attempted to steal a sack of
rice that was stacked in close proximity to the
open front door of the shop. Their efforts were
frustrated by the three shop assistants named Dong
Aue Sing (唐順生), Dong Foh Sung (唐福生) and
Lee Pak Ying (李伯英) respectively and the thieves
made good their escape.

About 5 minutes later a crowd of about 30 male
Chinese of the coolie class gathered outside the
shop and started shouting "Steal Rice" (Tsang Mei
(搶米)), and before the shop assistants could close
the shop door the mob rushed into the premises and
pulled down a stack of rice situated near the shop
door. The shop assistants tried to oppose the
thieves but they were easily overcome and unable
to prevent the mob from carrying away 14 sacks of
rice.

The thieves were in the shop for about five
minutes and most of them decamped into an alleyway
leading to Tsu Ka Ba Road, after which the shop
assistants closed the shop, and informed the
station.

At 11 a.m. 23/2/40 C. D. C. 183 whilst patrolling

1940年2月23日上午10:52，接到临清路106-8号阮丰 (Yuen Foong) 米店的电话留言，称两名苦力试图从店内偷走一袋大米未遂，随后逃脱。

然而，经查询查明以下情况。

1940年2月23日上午10:40左右，两名苦力阶层华籍男子试图偷走堆放在店铺敞开的前门附近的一袋大米。他们的企图被三名店员唐順生 (Dong Aue Sing)、唐福生 (Dong Foh Sung) 和李伯英 (Lee Pak Ying) 挫败，窃贼随即逃脱。

约5分钟后，一群约30名苦力阶层华籍男子聚集在店外，开始高喊“抢米” (Tsang Mei)，在店员来得及关闭店门前，这群暴徒冲进店内，推倒了位于店门附近的一堆大米。店员试图抵抗窃贼，但轻易被制服，无法阻止暴徒搬走14袋大米。

窃贼在店内停留约五分钟，随后大多数人逃入通往朱家浜路 (Tsu Ka Ba Road) 的一条弄堂，之后店员关闭了店铺，并向巡捕房报案。

Chinese running across a piece of vacant ground with a

The complt's assistants state that they have

Persons residing in the vicinity of the complt's shop

All rice shops in this district have been

一名华人肩扛一袋大米跑过一块空地。侦探喝令该男子停下，但他扔下大米后逃脱。这袋大米后来被投诉人的店员董方松 (Dong Fon Sung) 确认为从投诉人店铺被盗之物。

投诉人的店员表示他们以前从未见过这些窃贼，并认为他们并非附近居民。居住在投诉人店铺附近并目睹事发经过的居民在接受询问时也表达了类似看法。

在朱家浜路 (Tsu Ka Ba Road) 进行了进一步查询，但未获得能揭示罪犯身份和/或有助于追回大米的信息。

投诉人无视警方于1940年2月16日给予的建议，当时刑事侦缉小队警员108号曾警告他该地区近期发生米店抢劫案，并建议他加固店门。

本区所有米店均已获知此案，并再次被警告采取预防措施。

Subject Rice looting in Wayside District.
Made by D.I. Cumming. Forwarded by E. Trollope
Officer i/c.

Sir,
The following instances of rice and flour looting were reported at Wayside Station on 16-2-40:-
(1) At 7.15 a.m. on 16-2-40, about twenty male and female Chinese of the coolie class entered the Yue Tsung Rice Shop, 128 Alcock Road, owned by Wong Pao Ling. They scooped rice in to various containers which they had brought for the purpose. Complainant subsequently reported to the Police but the looters had gone on their arrival. It is estimated by the complainant that four piculs of rice were stolen.
(2) At 1.10 p.m. on 16-2-40, a crowd of about 50 or 60 male Chinese of the poorer class entered the Zung Yuen Rice Shop, 770 Tongshan Road, where by force of members they invaded the rear of the counter from where they removed a quantity of rice which they took away in various receptables which they brought for the purpose. Complainant telephoned the Station but on arrival of Police the looters had disappeared.
It is estimated by the complainant that two piculs of rice were stolen.
(3) At 2.20 p.m. on 16-2-40, a crowd of about 70 male and female Chinese entered the Nyi Tsong Rice Shop at 875 East Yuhang Road. They surged behind the counter and began to scoop rice and flour from bins and bags. Complainant telephoned the Station but on arrival of Police the looters had disappeared. It is estimated by the complainant that in all two piculs of rice and two bags of flour were stolen.
D. I.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
Section 1, Special Branch Station,
REPORT
Date, January 15, 1940.

Subject Situation of rice shops in Zao Ka Doo, Western District, O.O.L.

Made by. D.S.I. Liao Chung Chien Forwarded by. D.I. Crawford

The rice shops operating in the Zao Ka Doo,
Western District, O.O.L. have been selling rice through
half-open doors or through small holes in the shop
shutters in view of the prevalence of looting in that
area.

A "Shanghai Municipality Western District Rice
Merchants' Trade Association" (滬西區米商同業公會),
was recently formed at 93 Erenan Road, O.O.L. with
Wong Tse Woo (黃致和), ex-Commander of Zao Ka Doo
Merchants' Volunteer Corps (defunct) and a rice dealer,
as Chairman. Under his auspices a meeting was held
in the office between 2 p.m. and 4 p.m., January 11,
1940 when some 30 rice shop owners attended. The
following resolutions were discussed and passed:-

1. That an appeal be sent to the officer-in-charge
of the Western District Police Bureau for police
protection to the rice shops in Zao Ka Doo.

2. That the rice shops continue their business
through half-open doors until an assurance
of protection from the Western District Police
Bureau is obtained.

3. That the rice shops be warned to refrain
from hoarding in order to avoid a rise in
the price of the cereal.

Liao Chung Chien
D. S. I.

D.C. (Special Branch)

报告
日期，1940年1月15日。

主题 越界筑路西区曹家渡地区米店状况。

由 廖仲坚 (Liao Chung Chien) 高级督察撰写。由 Crawford 督察转呈。

鉴于该地区抢劫案频发，越界筑路西区曹家渡 (Zao Ka Doo) 地区的米店一直通过半开的店门或百叶窗上的小孔出售大米。

一家“沪西区米商同业公会”最近于越界筑路爱仁南路93号成立，由前曹家渡商人义勇队（已解散）指挥官兼米商黄致和 (Wong Tse Woo) 担任主席。在他的主持下，1940年1月11日下午2时至4时在办事处举行了一次会议，约有30名米店店主出席。讨论并通过了以下决议：-

1. 向西区警察局负责人发出呼吁，请求对曹家渡地区的米店提供警力保护。

2. 在获得西区警察局的保护保证之前，米店继续通过半开的店门营业。

3. 警告米店不要囤积居奇，以避免粮价上涨。

廖仲坚
高级督察。

SHANGHAI TIMES.

JAN 5 1940

GROUPS OF BEGGARS
RAID RICE SHOPS

Demand And Attempt
To Steal Rice; Cheap
Supplies For Poor

Rice shops in the Louza and
Sinza Police districts received a
scare yesterday morning when large
parties of beggars commenced
approaching them for donations of
rice. In some cases the beggars
became threatening, making de-
mands and even going as far as
attempting to steal rice and rice
cakes.
Police were called upon for assist-
ance and cleared away the mobs of
beggars, detaining several men for
a period and then releasing them.
At a conference held at 4 o'clock
yesterday afternoon, the Shanghai
Staple Food Regulation Committee
passed one of its most important
resolutions. This was the establish-
ment of a "Frumentation Com-
mission" (Ping tiao wei yuan hui),
whose task will be to distribute
large quantities of rice to the
destitute people of Shanghai, at
prices well below the present
market levels.
More than 30 Shanghai notables,
representing almost all the major
trades of local business including
banking, shipping, and other in-
terests, were present at the meeting.
Sixteen men, headed by Mr. Yu Ya-
ching, were nominated as the
organizing committee of the new
commission. It was also decided to
raise a fund of $1,000,000 as the
initial capital of the enterprise.

Lee

《字林西报》。

1940年1月5日

乞丐团伙
袭击米店

索要并企图
窃取大米；为穷人
提供廉价供应

昨天上午，老闸和新闸巡捕房辖区内的米店受到惊吓，大批乞丐开始向他们索要大米捐赠。在某些情况下，乞丐变得具有威胁性，提出要求，甚至企图窃取大米和年糕。
警方被召来协助，驱散了乞丐群，拘留了几名男子一段时间后将其释放。
在昨天下午4点举行的会议上，上海主食管理委员会通过了其最重要的决议之一。即成立“平粜委员会” (Ping tiao wei yuan hui)，其任务是以远低于当前市场水平的价格向上海的贫民分发大量大米。
三十多位上海名流出席了会议，他们代表了当地商业几乎所有主要行业，包括银行、航运及其他利益集团。十六人被提名为新委员会的组织委员会成员，由于亚钦 (Yu Ya-ching) 先生领衔。会议还决定筹集100万美元作为该企业的启动资金。

Lee
C 3/1

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of WONG ZOO SS.
native of Soochow taken by C.D.
Ch. Rd. Stn. on the 18-12-39 and translated by Clerk Tan.

At about 10.50a.m. on the 16-12-39, my husband Wong Sz Kung was arrested by Police in connection with a riot at the San Mau Rice Shop, 125 Chengtu Road and subsequently escorted to Police Station.

At about 10a.m. on the 18-12-39, while making a purchase from a sauce shop on Chengtu Road, I heard pedestrians talk about the death of my husband that he had succumbed to his injuries received in the riot.

However, at 12 noon 18-12-39, my husband came back home. I told him what I heard it rumoured that he had died from the injuries in the riot. He then told me that after arrest, he was taken to Chengtu Road Police Station and on 18-12-39 he was arraigned before the Court and sentenced to 3 months' imprisonment suspended for 2 years. He further told me that in the course of trial, he was warned by the presiding judge not to create any further disturbance. I now realize that the above rumour concerning the death of my husband was absolutely groundless, I do not know where it originated from.

At about 3p.m. same date, we were summoned to Chengtu Road Police Station by detectives to whom we confirmed the fact that the above rumour had been in circulation and now further realized that same was false.

Signed and crossmarked.

1939年12月16日上午10时50分左右，我丈夫王世根因涉及成都路125号三茂米店的骚乱被警察逮捕，随后被押送至警察局。

1939年12月18日上午10时左右，我在成都路一家酱园购物时，听到路人谈论我丈夫的死讯，说他在骚乱中因伤身亡。

然而，1939年12月18日中午12时，我丈夫回到家中。我告诉他我听到的关于他因骚乱受伤而死的谣言。他随后告诉我，被捕后他被带到成都路警察局，并于1939年12月18日出庭受审，被判处监禁三个月，缓刑两年。他还告诉我，在审判过程中，主审法官警告他不得再制造任何骚乱。我现在意识到上述关于我丈夫死亡的谣言毫无根据，我不知道谣言源自何处。

同日大约下午3时，我们被侦探传唤至成都路警察局，向他们确认上述谣言一直在流传，并进一步认识到该谣言是虚假的。

1.

Rice Situation - Central District.

Sir,

The rice situation in the Central District remained quite normal during the twenty-four hours ending December 17.

Although no serious disturbances took place and no attempt was made to plunder any of the rice shops, it is, however, believed that one mob did filter into the district in a surreptitious manner during the afternoon for this purpose.

At 3.50p.m. C.C.R. reported that a large crowd had assembled in the vicinity of the Hain Teh Rice Shop (新泰米店), 135 Ningpo Road.

The mob consisted of Kompo females and young children and several males of the loafer class.

All were reported to have carried sacks and other receptacles suitable for the carrying of rice.

These people are definitely not Central residents and are believed to have come from the Western Area.

They made "attempt to rush the shop and stood in a group some twenty or thirty yards away.

Vigilance by Police on duty in the vicinity and the subsequent arrival of reinforcements apparently discouraged the mob who broke up and are reported to

Remarks
(Any outstanding or peculiar feature to be
commented on by investigating officer).

Between 11-15am. and 4-15pm. on 10/12/39
there were 13 instances of looting and attempted
looting of Rice Shops in the Sinza District, as
follows:

(1) At 11-15am. a telephone message was received from
a Rice Shop at No.886 Sinza Road reporting a large
crowd of male and female Chinese attempting to loot
the shop.
A Party of Police attended and dispersed the
crowd, who had failed to steal anything.
Complainant: Wong Vung Kyi(黃鳳麒).

(2) At 11-20am. a telephone message was received from
a Rice Shop at No.323-5 Shanhaikwan Road reporting a
crowd looting the premises.
A Party of Police attended and dispersed the
crowd, who had not succeeded in stealing anything.
Complainant: Tseu Pau Ling(朱宝林).

(3) At 11-20am. a telephone message was received from
a Rice Shop at No. 337 Shanhaikwan Road, reporting
a crowd looting the shop.
The Party of Police attending succeeded in
dispersing the crowd and it was later learnt that
rice to the value of $8.00 had been stolen. No
arrests were made.
Complainant: Yih Sz Kau(叶士高).

(4) At 1-15pm. a telephone message was received from a
Rice Shop at No.372 Medhurst Road reporting a crowd
looting the premises, and a party of Police attended
and succeeded in dispersing the crowd, arresting
five persons, as follows:-

1939年12月10日上午11时15分至下午4时15分之间，新闸区发生了13起米店抢劫和企图抢劫事件，具体如下：

(1) 上午11时15分，接到新闸路886号一家米店的电话消息，报告有一大群男女华人试图抢劫该店。
一队警察到场并驱散了人群，他们未能偷走任何东西。
投诉人：Wong Vung Kyi（黃鳳麒）。

(2) 上午11时20分，接到山海关路323-5号一家米店的电话消息，报告有一群人在抢劫该场所。
一队警察到场并驱散了人群，他们未能成功偷走任何东西。
投诉人：Tseu Pau Ling（朱宝林）。

(3) 上午11时20分，接到山海关路337号一家米店的电话消息，报告有一群人在抢劫该店。
到场的警察小队成功驱散了人群，后获悉价值8.00美元的大米被盗。未实施逮捕。
投诉人：Yih Sz Kau（叶士高）。

(4) 下午1时15分，接到麦赫斯特路（Medhurst Road）372号一家米店的电话消息，报告有一群人在抢劫该场所，一队警察到场并成功驱散人群，逮捕了五人，如下：-

16.12.39.

Rice Riots in the Peetoo Road District on 16.12.39.

At 9 a.m. 16.12.39. in response to a telephone message from the
Wan Kong (萬康) Rice Shop, 1395-7 Ferry Road, to the effect that a riot
was in progress at the shop, a party of Police under Inspector Watson,
Officer in charge, immediately turned out. On arrival of Police, the
rioters had already been dispersed and most of them had escaped with a
large number sacks of rice, stolen from the shop. Police party,
however, was able to overtake a part of the offenders, effecting the
arrest of sixteen male Chinese, four females and one boy and recovery
of a quantity of rice, approximately 5 sacks from them.

The owner of the shop named Wong Ziang Ching (吳祥慶), estimated
that a total loss of 30 sacks of rice valued at $600.00 was suffered
as the result of the riot. There were, however, no casualties.

A separate list of the description of the arrested persons is
attached.

Six other rice shops were broken into by the rioters throughout
the day and owing to the prompt arrival of Police party at the scene of
each riot on receipt of information, the mob dispersed, having no
opportunity to loot anything from the shop. In one of these attempts,
a male Chinese named Wong Toh Hee (汪德喜), aged 41, native of Anhwei,
S/coolie residing straw hut, Yah S Loong, off Ferry Road, who was
attempting to break into a rice shop with a sharp iron hook, which was
found to be in his possession at the time of his arrest, was arrested
by Police.

The following are the shops which had been broken into by the
rioters and nothing was stolen from the shops:

11.45 a.m. - Yung Foong (永豐) Rice Shop, 68-70 Robison Rd, O.O.L
12.40 p.m. - Hung Foong (恒豐) Rice Shop, 18 Penang Road.
2.04 p.m. - Kung Ping (公平) Rice Shop, 4655 Robison Road.

3.38 p.m. - Dong Zung Ziang (同盛祥) Rice Shop, 495 Ichang Rd.
5.07 p.m. - Dong Fah Ziang (同發祥) Rice Shop, 1426 Ferry Rd.

A total of 22 persons were arrested by Police and they were
detained at the station, pending instructions from D.O. "B" Division.

1939年12月16日毕陡路 (Peetoo Road) 地区发生米骚乱。

1939年12月16日上午9时，接万康 (Wan Kong) 米店（斐伦路1395-7号）电话消息，称该店正在发生骚乱，由督察 Watson 率领的一队警员立即出动。警员抵达时，暴徒已散去，大多数人携带从店内偷窃的大量袋装大米逃逸。然而，警队能够追上部分违法者，逮捕了16名中国男性、4名女性和1名男孩，并从他们手中追回了约5袋大米。

店主吴祥慶 (Wong Ziang Ching) 估计，骚乱导致总共损失30袋大米，价值$600.00。不过，没有人员伤亡。

另附被捕人员特征清单。

当天另有六家米店被暴徒闯入，但由于警队在接到消息后迅速抵达各骚乱现场，人群解散，未有机会从店内抢劫任何东西。在其中一次企图作案中，一名名为汪德喜 (Wong Toh Hee) 的中国男性，41岁，安徽籍，单身/苦力，居住在斐伦路近亚斯龙 (Yah S Loong) 的草棚，企图用尖锐铁钩撬开一家米店，被捕时该铁钩在其身上被发现，遂被警方逮捕。

Enquiries by D.S. Taylor and C.D.C. 26.

Owing to the tense situation prevailing, due
to the excessive price of rice and other commodities,
precautionary measures were adopted with a view to
preventing breaches of the peace. C.P.C.s were
posted at all rice shops in the district with ins-
tructions to immediately inform the station, where
reserves were standing-by, in the event of large
crowds collecting in the vicinity of rice shops and
refusing to disperse, when ordered to do so by the
officers on duty at these places.

At 10.33 a.m. 16-12-39 telephone message (St.
Tel. Box 5) was received from C.P.S. 491, on behalf
of C.P.C. 976 reporting that a large crowd of male
and female Chinese had collected in the vicinity of
the Ziang Zung (祥順) Rice shop, 12-14 Chungking
Road. The C.P.C. had ordered the loiterers to dis-
perse but they moved from one place to another and
remained. He further reported that the crowd was
starting to get out of hand and he expected a dis-
turbance.

S.I.s Moffat and Wilkinson, Inspector Yao Chia
Kwei, D.S. Taylor and party of Uniform and detectives
immediately proceeded to the scene and dispersed
the mob, without any untoward incident. The shop
was instructed to put up their wooden shutters and
to make transactions through the small grille window.
Police were reinforced at this place and the party
left to visit other rice shops in the district.

Whilst returning to the station, it was observed

鉴于因大米及其他商品价格过高而导致的紧张局势，已采取预防措施以防止破坏和平的行为发生。巡捕被派驻于本区所有米店，并奉命指示：一旦有大量人群在米店附近聚集，且经现场执勤警官命令解散而拒绝服从时，须立即通知警局，届时后备警力将待命出动。

1939年12月16日上午10时33分，接到来自第491号中国巡捕（C.P.S. 491）的电话留言（通过圣部电话箱5号），代表第976号中国巡捕（C.P.C. 976）报告称，大量中国男女民众聚集在重庆路12-14号祥顺（Ziang Zung）米店附近。该中国巡捕已命令闲散人员解散，但这些人从一处移至另一处，并未离去。他还报告称，人群开始失控，他预计会发生骚乱。

副督察莫法特（Moffat）和威尔金森（Wilkinson）、姚家桂（Yao Chia Kwei）督察、警佐泰勒（Taylor）及其率领的一队制服警员和便衣侦探立即赶赴现场，驱散了暴民，未发生任何意外事件。该店奉命放下木制百叶窗，并通过小格栅窗口进行交易。该地点的警力得到增援，随后该队人员离开，前往视察本区的其他米店。

After the crowd had been dispersed and order res-tored the San Mau rice shop checked their stocks and found a loss of 40 bags of flour each weighing 49 lbs and to the total value of $400.00, had been forcibly re-moved from the shop,

It was noticed that during this raid, there were not a few students mingling with the crowd and one student Fee Kyi Sung (費歧生), 27, Shanghai, M/student, San woo (三友) University Night School, Jinkee Road, residing at 10/47 Chengtu Road was arrested and brought to the station for enquiries. He was later released, as there was not sufficient evidence to establish defi-nite connection with the riot.

由负责警官率领的一队警察立即前往处置。抵达现场后，发现大量人群聚集在上述米店外，其中大多数为围观者。

警察抵达之时，拥挤在店内的一些人向不同方向逃散。以下列名人员是在店内实际被捕的：—

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

The 5th, 6th & 7th named will be released after curfew hours, these people being of the beggars class against whom no evidence of attempting larceny can be obtained.

With the regards to the 8th and 9th named, hereinafter referred to as the 1st & the 2nd accused, have been definitely identified by the shop assistants named Wong Kou Tseng (王國珍) and Sung Ping Yuen (沈尚元) as those who were actually attempting to steal the rice which was stored in sacks and piled against the rear walls of the shop. There two men were seen to pull the sacks and to open same, thereby allowing many persons, who had escaped, to steal the rice.

The complainant reports that in all, 5 sacks of rice valued at approximately $175.00 was stolen by these unknown persons.

On instruction of D.O. "C" the 1st and 2nd accused have been charged with contrary to Art. 321 of C.C.C. and will before the S.S.D. Court on 18-12-39.

At 5:30 p.m. 14.12.39., a telephone message
was received from the Zung Tai (仁泰) Rice Shop,
No.1789 Robison Road, to the effect that a large
crowd were stealing rice.

The Station alarm was sounded and a party of
police and detectives with Inspector Watson i/c.
attended.

On the arrival of the police party, the
thieves had already been dispersed by P.S.84 Vankoff
and a uniform search party and Hav. Trooper 503,
Sikh Troopers 382, 424, 123 and 658, who arrived on
the scene a few minutes previously.

Hav. 503 and Sikh Trooper 382 effected the
arrest of the 1st and 2nd accused about 100 yards
from the rice shop in the act of taking away a sack
of rice.

An immediate search of the vicinity resulted
in F.S. 363 MacAuley arresting the 3rd and 4th
accused in a nearby alleyway with a sack of rice
in their possession. Nine other sacks of rice were
found abandoned on the roadway and in adjoining
alleyways.

One named Tsau Ching Fong (焦金芳), age 42,
native of Chinkiang, M/hawker, residing No.1606 Hart
Road, was arrested by P.S. Vankoff on suspicion of
being concerned, but was released on completion of
enquiries.

Further enquiries by detectives revealed that
at about 5:10 p.m. even date, about 20 to 30 persons
of the poor class came to the complainant's shop
and asked for rice and on being refused, rushed into

警局发出警报，由沃森（Watson）巡官率领的一队警员和侦探前往处置。

当警队抵达时，窃贼已被此前几分钟到达现场的84号警士万科夫（Vankoff）及一支制服搜查队、503号印籍骑警、以及382、424、123和658号锡克骑警驱散。

503号印籍骑警和382号锡克骑警在距离米行约100码处，逮捕了正在搬走一袋大米的第一和第二被告。

对附近区域的立即搜查导致363号外籍警员麦考利（MacAuley）在附近的一条小巷中逮捕了持有一袋大米的第三和第四被告。在路面及相邻的小巷中发现了九袋被遗弃的大米。

一名叫焦金芳（Tsau Ching Fong），42岁，镇江籍，职业：小贩，住址：赫德路（Hart Road）1606号，被84号警士万科夫以涉嫌参与为由逮捕，但在问询结束后获释。

经侦探进一步调查得知，同日约下午5时10分，约有20至30名贫民来到报案人的店铺索要大米，在被拒绝后，冲入

from the Dong Meu (同茂) Rice Shop, No. 959 Ferry Road, to the effect

ing rice. A party under Officer i/c attended to find a large crowd

of the police, but none were found to have possession of rice. It

1939年12月15日下午5时48分，接到来电，报称位于渡船路（Ferry Road）959号的同茂米店遭一群暴民闯入抢米。由负责警官率领的一队警员前往处置，发现店前聚集了大量人群，这些人在警察接近时四散而去，但无人被发现持有大米。看来，实际作案者在行窃时被中央捕房第1300号巡警惊扰，但仍成功盗走10袋大米，价值350.00元。

负责警员对该米店附近的整个区域进行了搜查，但未实施任何逮捕或追回赃物。

同日（即1939年12月15日）下午5时20分，接到来电，报称位于罗宾森路（Robison Road）401号的長泰米店发生骚乱，外侨越界筑路区（O.O.L.）。由沃森（Watson）巡官率领的一队警员前往处置，发现一群人聚集在店门前搅闹，他们已拆毁铁栅栏和百叶窗。暴民被驱散，十二名男子，即：

(1) 張奧方 (Tsang Shing Fong)；34岁，南京籍，男，店员，住罗宾森路437号。
(2) 李心霞 (Lee Sing Yah)；38岁，安徽籍，男，苦力，住罗宾森路8号。
(3) 王月樓 (Wong Yue Leu)；26岁，广东籍，男，黄包车夫，住外侨越界筑路区（O.O.L.）。
(4) 吳維寶 (Woo Vee Pau)；16岁，广东籍，男，苦力，住罗宾森路437号。
(5) 徐國慶 (Zee Koh Ching)；27岁，广东籍，男，苦力，住外侨越界筑路区（O.O.L.）。
(6) 余慶華 (Yue Ching Hwa)；23岁，广东籍，男，苦力，住外侨越界筑路区（O.O.L.）。
(7) 汪慶堂 (Waung Ching Daung)；32岁，广东籍，男，店员，住罗宾森路354号。
(8) 姚清奎 (Yao Zei Kwei)；17岁，广东籍，男，苦力，住罗宾森路旁草棚。
(9) 董元龍 (Toong Yuen Loong)；41岁，广东籍，男，苦力，住罗宾森路永安里1号。
(10) 陳和包 (Zung Woo Pao)；19岁，广东籍，男，学徒，住罗宾森路369号。
(11) 曾文基 (Tsang Vung Kyi)；17岁，广东籍，男，苦力，住罗宾森路。
(12) 黃地發 (Wong Dee Fah)；30岁，广东籍，男，苦力，住罗宾森路。

因无法逃脱，被发现藏匿于成堆的袋装大米之中，随后被带至警局。

据报该店被盗十袋大米，价值300.00元。

根据“B”分区副主管的指示，上述十二名被捕人员将被拘留过夜，并于1939年12月16日上午释放。

鉴于不打算进行逮捕或追回赃物，本人建议将这些案件归档保存，以备日后查考。

高级侦探督察    “B”分区副主管    D.S. 326.

REPORT

Subject... Death of a chinese female named Dzang Zung Sz (陳成氏) - knocked
down by a mob attempting to rob rice.

Made by. D...I. TAO KONG YONG. Forwarded by.................... Officer i/c.

Sir,

At 5:10 p.m. on 15-12-39 a telephone message was
received to the effect that a big crowd of people
attempting to break into the Lao Yung Foong (老永源)
Rice Shop, 1309 Penang Road. The message was received
simultaneously by this station and Pootoo Road, but the
scene was first attended by a party of detectives and
uniform men under S.I. Barton of Pootoo Road Station.
In the course of charge, the crowd dispersed and rushed
into King Sui Li, off Penang Road where the mob knocked
down the following persons, residents of the said alleyway.

1) Dzang Zung Sz (陳成氏), 53, Yangchow, H/Female,
72 King Sui Li off Penang Road,
2) Nyi Yue Sz (倪俞氏), 67, Kompo, Widow, No.72
King Sui Li off Penang Road,
3) Li Mao Dee (李毛弟), 12, Kompo, S/Female,
No.250 King Sui Li off Penang Road,
4) Pan Tsong Ling (潘忠林), 14, Kompo, S/Male,
No.255.King Sui Li, off Penang Road,
5) Liu Dah Ching (刘大俊), 12, Kompo, S/Female,
No. 20 King Sui Li, off Penang Road,
6) Koo Woo Sa (高吳氏), 47, Yangchow, H/Female,
No.80 King Sui Li, off Penang Road.

The above persons were certified by Labour Hospital
to have suffered the following injuries:-

1) Trampled to Death.
2) Scalded on left leg by hot water.
3) Scalded on left leg by hot water.
4) Laceration of scalp.
5) Laceration of left cheek and chin.
6) Contusion of chest.

SHANGHAI TIMES!
DEC 1 7 1939

Rice Riots Continue In
Force Yesterday Despite
Precautions Of Police

Investigations Reveal Disturbances Caused By
Hooligans Rather Than Hungry Mobs; Dealer
Wounded By Gunman; Over 20 Cases Reported

DECISION TO REDUCE PRICES OF RICE
MADE AT IMPORTANT CONFERENCE

Despite the fact that strong precautions were being taken
by the police authorities in the International Settlement and
the French Concession for the protection of the rice hongs,
about 20 riots were staged yesterday morning and afternoon in
the two foreign areas. Police turned out in most of the cases
to disperse the crowds and a number of arrests were made in
several instances.

Investigation revealed that in most cases the riots were
not staged as the result of people going hungry or crowds being
specially organized. In the majority of the cases an argument
would start in a rice hong between a customer and the assist-
ants over the price of the staple or the weight given. Crowds
would gather around and a number of hooligans, taking advant-
age of the opportunity, would rush into the store and commence
looting.

In most of the incidents the
crowds would clear prior to the
arrival of the police, after having
stolen as much rice as they could
possibly carry away. There were
also a number of false alarms
regarding rice riots, panicky rice
shop proprietors calling for police
assistance as soon as some customer
began to raise his voice.

Dealer Wounded

Mr. Shen Zeng-ven, 63-year-old
rice broker, was wounded in the
arm by one of two gunmen, who
stopped him outside the Foochow
Road Market at about 10 o'clock
yesterday morning, while he was
riding in his private ricksha. Whe-
ther the attempted assassination of
Mr. Shen has anything to do with
the rice riots or the general rice
situation or not, has not as yet been
definitely established.

Mr. Shen was stopped by two
men, one of whom produced a pistol
and fired one shot and then ran
off with his accomplice. An alarm
was raised, but by the time the
police arrived, the gunmen had
already escaped. Mr. Shen was re-
moved to hospital in an ambulance.

21 Arrests

Among the 20 rice riots reported
in the Settlement and the French
Concession yesterday, arrests were
only made in three cases. In the
first riot reported in the morning
at 1397 Ferry Road, 21 arrests
were made by a party of police,
who turned out from Pootoo Road
Police Station. The riot was stag-
ed at about 9 o'clock, a large num-
ber of bags being carried out from
the shop by the looting mob. The
police party arrived on the scene
in quick order, arrested 21 men
and recovered the majority of the
stolen rice.

Nine arrests were made in the
West Emergency Station following an
attack on a hong at 208 Kaifeng
Road at 10 a.m.

Other riots were staged at the
following shops:—
10.50 a.m., 126 Chengtu Road.
11.20 a.m., 291 Taku Road.
11.30 a.m., 222 Shanhaikwan Rd
11.40 a.m., 389 Burkill Road.
11.40 a.m., 66 Taku Road.
2.40 p.m., 65 Connaught Road.
5.07 p.m., 1438 Ferry Road.
One arrest by police, nothing
stolen.

Between 3.35 and 5.15 p.m.: at
30 Talung Road, 585 Myburgh Road,
618 Tatung Road, 149 Tsingtao
Road and 542 Myburgh Road.

Besides, these six more cases of
rice looting occurred yesterday in
the French Concession. They are
listed as follows:—
Tin Tai Rice Store, 128 Rue Bour-
geat, at 10.10 a.m.
Loss:—about 120 piculs of 160
catties each.

At 287 Rue Ratard. Loss:—about
13 piculs.
Kung Ta Rice Store, 98 Albert
Road. Loss about 12 piculs.
Teh Yi Tai Rice Store, 66 Avenue
Dubail.
At 120 Rue Gaston Kahn.
At the corner of Rue du Marche
and Rue Lafayette.

Three Injured

Three rioters sustained lacera-
tions of the scalp following a riot
staged in the Chengtu Road Police
district yesterday morning. They
were injured during the time that
the police were dispersing a crowd
and making arrests. The three men
are being detained at the Police
Hospital.

Conference Takes Place

Three representatives were sent by
the Shanghai Rice Stores Guild and
four were sent by the Shanghai
Beans and Rice Guild to call on the
Deputy Secretary of the S.M.C., Mr.
T. K. Ho, at 10 o'clock yesterday
morning. They requested the au-
thorities to render adequate pro-
tection to legitimate merchants
against the looting mobs, and also
discussed the problem of price
control.

It was understood that at this
conference, the rice merchants and
S.M.C. both agreed to reduce the
maximum permissible price of first
grade rice from $45 to $40, and for
next-grade rice from $38 to $33, re-
presenting a cut of $5 each.

An executive meeting of the
Shanghai Beans and Rice Guild was
called later yesterday, at 4 p.m.
Two important resolutions were
passed. The first was to approve
the new lower price limits of $40
and $33 as arranged between the
Guild's representatives and the
S.M.C. The second was to send
a formal communication to the
S.M.C. asking that adequate pro-
tection be accorded to honest and
legitimate merchants against libel
and mobs.

A proclamation was issued by the
guild yesterday to the effect that,
beginning from to-day, no first qua-
lity white rice shall be allowed to
sell in excess of $40, and that next
grade rice shall not be sold in excess
of $33. The proclamation added
that imported foreign rice, owing
to fluctuations in foreign exchange,
will be temporary exempt from this
rule.

No Market Yesterday

The rice market on Foochow Road
failed to open yesterday as only a
few traders were present and there
was no offer or bid. Throughout
the morning not a single transaction
was made. There is no market in
the afternoon. Fear of the wide-
spread rice riots was said to be the
reason for the absence of transac-
tions.

1939年12月17日

尽管警方采取预防措施
昨日米骚乱仍猛烈持续

调查显示骚乱系由流氓引发而非饥民；
商贩遭枪手枪击受伤；报案逾20起

重要会议决定降低米价

尽管公共租界和法租界的警察当局已采取严密措施保护米行，但昨天上午和下午，这两个外侨区域仍发生了约20起骚乱。在大多数案件中，警方出动驱散人群，并在数起事件中实施了逮捕。

调查显示，在大多数情况下，骚乱并非因人们挨饿或人群经过特别组织而引发。在多数案件中，争执始于米行内顾客与店员之间，起因是主粮价格或称量重量问题。人群随即聚集，一些流氓趁机冲入店内开始抢劫。

在大多数事件中，人群在抢走尽可能多的大米后，会在警察到达前散去。此外，还出现了一些关于米骚乱的虚假警报，恐慌的米店店主只要听到有顾客提高嗓门，便立即呼叫警方援助。

商贩受伤

63岁的米业经纪人沈增文（Shen Zeng-ven，音译）先生，昨天上午10点左右，当他乘坐私人黄包车经过福州路市场外时，被两名枪手中的其中一人击中手臂。沈先生遇刺是否与米骚乱或整体米市局势有关，目前尚未确定。

沈先生被两名男子拦下，其中一人掏出手枪开了一枪，随后与同伙逃跑。虽然有人报警，但当警察赶到时，枪手已经逃脱。沈先生由救护车送往医院。

21人被捕

在昨日公共租界和法租界报告的20起米骚乱中，仅在三起案件中实施了逮捕。在上午报告的第一起骚乱中，地点位于渡船路1397号，一支从普陀路警察局出动的警队逮捕了21人。骚乱发生在9点左右，大量米袋被抢劫暴徒从店内搬出。警队迅速赶到现场，逮捕了21名男子，并追回了大部分被盗大米。

上午10点，开封路208号一家米行遭到袭击后，西区紧急警局（West Emergency Station）逮捕了九人。

其他骚乱发生在以下店铺：—
上午10:50，成都路126号。
上午11:20，大沽路291号。
上午11:30，山海关路222号。
上午11:40，伯基尔路（Burkill Road）389号。
上午11:40，大沽路66号。
下午2:40，康纳路（Connaught Road）65号。
下午5:07，渡船路1438号。
警方逮捕一人，无财物丢失。

下午3:35至5:15之间：达隆路（Talung Road）30号，迈burgh路（Myburgh Road）585号，大同路618号，青岛路149号和迈burgh路（Myburgh Road）542号。

此外，昨日法租界还发生了另外六起米粮抢劫案。列举如下：—
宝嘉路（Rue Bourgeat）128号，金泰米店，上午10:10。
损失：—约120担，每担160斤。

拉塔德路（Rue Ratard）287号。损失：—约13担。
公大米店，亚尔培路（Albert Road）98号。损失约12担。
德义泰米店，杜美路（Avenue Dubail）66号。
加斯东·卡恩路（Rue Gaston Kahn）120号。
市场路（Rue du Marche）与拉斐特路（Rue Lafayette）转角处。

三人受伤

昨天上午在成都路警察辖区发生的一起骚乱中，三名骚乱者头皮撕裂受伤。他们在警方驱散人群和实施逮捕期间受伤。这三名男子正被羁押在警察医院。

召开会议

上海米业公会派出三名代表，上海豆米业公会派出四名代表，于昨天上午10点拜访工部局副秘书何德奎（T. K. Ho）先生。他们请求当局对合法商人提供充分保护，以防抢劫暴徒侵害，并讨论了价格管制问题。

据悉，在此次会议上，米商和工部局双方同意将一等白米的最高允许价格从45元降至40元，次等米从38元降至33元，即各降低5元。

上海豆米业公会随后于昨天下午4点召开执行会议。通过了两项重要决议。第一项是批准公会代表与工部局商定的40元和33元的新低价限额。第二项是向工部局发出正式函件，要求对诚实合法的商人提供充分保护，使其免受诽谤和暴民侵害。

公会昨天发布告示，称从今天起，一等白米售价不得超过40元，次等米售价不得超过33元。告示补充说，由于外汇波动，进口洋米将暂时豁免于此规定。

昨日无交易

福州路的米市昨日未能开市，因为只有少数交易者到场，且无人出价或还价。整个上午没有达成任何交易。下午也没有市场。据说，对 widespread 米骚乱的恐惧是导致没有交易的原因。

page_data.en:
27863
SHANGHAI MERCURY
6 39
Ten Riots Staged
During Morning,
Police Kept Busy
Mobs Given Incitement
By Proclamation,
Says Dealer
$31,000 WORTH
TAKEN IN DAY
SMP Handle Outbreaks
On Outside Roads
In Neat Manner
While the Japanese conspicuously failed in their promises to bring China rice into Shanghai, riots over the grain which started yesterday afternoon continued this morning, when seven outbreaks were reported in the Settlement and three in the Concession and one rice dealer was wounded in an assassination attempt.
Police were on the alert and nipped more than one outbreak in the bud, but in other cases the rioters got away. In one instance with $400 of the grain which they removed in rickshas.
Big Loss
No less than 785 zah of rice, worth approximately $31,000, were taken in the riots yesterday afternoon. Figures are not available for this morning's efforts, but it is believed that they are very much below this amount.
Twenty-one Chinese were arrested in a riot at 1397 Ferry Road today, when police succeeded in regaining most of the stolen grain. One or two other arrests were made during the morning.
Dealer Wounded
Shen Zang-ven, 63 years old rice broker with offices at 145 Chekiang Road, was wounded in the arm at 10 a.m., as he was travelling in his ricksha along Foochow Road, outside the market.
Two men stepped from the sidewalk, fired at Mr. Shen and then made their escape. One bullet hit him in the arm and fractured it. Motive for the attack has not as yet been discovered. First reports that Mr. Shen had been one of the six put "on the mat" by the SMP Thursday were later found to be untrue.
Incited
Despite a letter from the SMC, announced in today's press, to the Shanghai Rice Retail Dealers' Association stating that the Councils' proclamation was not directed against members of the association in their legitimate business, but against manipulators and speculators, it is believed in some quarters that the proclamation has served to incite the crowds against rice shops in general. Prices, which have dropped on a "scare" at the proclamation, may rise if dealers refuse to buy more Saigon grain.
Extra police protection has been arranged for rice shops, but in view of the number of the latter, crowds have been able to stage many attacks in the last day or so.
Twenty Cents
Methods of rioters yesterday were noted by their demands for twenty cents' worth of rice, which shops refused, saying that $1 was the lowest unit. The mob thereupon would storm the shop and help itself.
Attempts of this sort at 501 Great Western Road and at 667 Jessfield Road failed when the SMP arrived in time, made the crowd form up in queues, and instructed the stores to sell each man his twenty cents' worth. Ta Tao police were interested spectators in the art of handling crowds.
Not Instigated
A Shanghai Municipal Council official told the Evening Post this morning that no reports had yet been received that the riots has been "instigated affairs."
It was pointed out that a true motive was lacking for the attacks as since the joint proclamation was issued at the beginning of this week by the SMC and FMC, prices for "gan mee" and Saigon rice had dropped more than $10.
Price Drop
The day before the joint proclamation was issued, the Council official explained, the price of rice was around $48 to $50 per picul, while this morning's prices stood at $39 per picul, with Saigon rice selling at $34.50 per picul.
Since December 1, the visible stock of rice in Shanghai had increased from 260,000 piculs to 358,000 piculs. This, the SMC official stated, was largely due to increasing supplies coming from Saigon, where large purchase orders had been placed last month and were now arriving in the city.

27863
《上海泰晤士报》
1939年6月
十起骚乱发生
警方晨间忙碌
商人称布告煽动暴民
价值31,000美元
一日之内被劫
工部局警务处
在外围道路
妥善处置爆发事件

尽管日本人在将大米运入上海的承诺上明显未能兑现，但始于昨天下午的粮食骚乱今天上午仍在继续，租界内报告了七起爆发事件，公共租界外（注：此处原文Concession通常指法租界，但在工部局档案语境中有时混用，结合上下文“Outside Roads”及SMP管辖范围，此处可能指越界筑路区域或泛指非核心区域，依惯例译作相关区域或保留原意，鉴于后文提到Ta Tao警察，此处应指涉及华界或交界处的混乱）报告了三起，另有一名米商在暗杀企图中受伤。

警方保持警戒，将不止一起骚乱消灭在萌芽状态，但在其他情况下，暴徒得以逃脱。在其中一起事件中，他们用手推车运走了价值400美元的粮食。

重大损失

昨天下午的骚乱中，不少于785石大米被抢走，价值约31,000美元。今天上午的损失数据尚不可得，但据信远低于此数额。

今天，在渡船路1397号发生的一起骚乱中，二十一名中国人被捕，警方成功追回了大部分被盗粮食。上午期间还有一两起其他逮捕行动。

商人受伤

沈藏文（Shen Zang-ven，音译），63岁，米行经纪人，办公地点位于浙江路145号，上午10时在乘人力车经过市场外的福州路时，手臂受伤。

两名男子从人行道上走出，向沈先生开枪，随后逃逸。一颗子弹击中其手臂并导致骨折。袭击动机尚未查明。早先有报告称沈先生是周四被工部局警务处“传唤训诫”（on the mat）的六人之一，后证实不实。

受煽动

尽管工部局在今日报刊上刊登了一封致上海米业零售同业公会的信函，声明理事会的布告并非针对该会成员的合法经营，而是针对操纵者和投机者，但某些方面认为，该布告已起到煽动人群反对一般米店的作用。因对布告感到恐慌而下跌的价格，如果经销商拒绝购买更多西贡大米，可能会回升。

已为米店安排了额外的警力保护，但鉴于米店数量众多，在过去一天左右的时间里，人群仍得以发动多次攻击。

二十分钱

昨天暴徒的手法体现在他们要求购买价值二十分钱的大米，米店拒绝，称最低销售单位为1美元。暴徒随即冲击店铺并自行拿取。

在大西路501号和极司菲尔路667号发生的此类企图，因工部局警务处及时赶到而失败，警方令人群排队，并指示商店向每人出售价值二十分钱的大米。大陶（Ta Tao，音译，可能指大场或当地警署）警察饶有兴致地旁观了这种处理人群的艺术。

非受指使

一位上海公共租界工部局官员今晨告诉《晚邮报》，尚未收到任何关于骚乱是“受指使事件”的报告。

有人指出，袭击缺乏真正的动机，因为自本周初工部局和法公董局发布联合布告以来，“粘米”和西贡大米的价格已下跌超过10美元。

价格下跌

这位工部局官员解释说，在联合布告发布的前一天，大米价格约为每担48至50美元，而今天上午的价格为每担39美元，西贡大米售价为每担34.50美元。

自12月1日以来，上海可见的大米库存已从26万担增加到35.8万担。这位工部局官员表示，这主要是由于来自西贡的供应增加，上月在那里下达的大额采购订单现在正陆续抵达本市。

27850
CHINA PRESS
1939

Fifty Nabbed
In 24 Rice
Riots Here

Cereal Worth: $40,000
Stolen By Looters As
Wave Continues

Twenty-four rice riots, including three in Frenchtown, occurred yesterday between 9 a.m. and midnight alone, when more than 800 piculs of rice, valued at more than $40,000, were stolen and more than 50 persons arrested.

With the police doing everything in their power to give ample protection to rice hongs, the riots were quelled in several instances, when police squads forced crowds to form orderly queues outside the shops.

It is a "physical impossibility, however, to post extra guards at the entrance to every rice shop, and while added police protection has been given hongs in the more secluded districts of the city, riots continued unabated yesterday.

Disorders Reach Peak

Disorders reached their peak when Mr. Shen Zang-ven, 63, rich rice merchant with offices at 145 Chekiang Road, was wounded in the arm at 10 a.m., when two men opened fire at him as he was traveling along Foochow Road by private ricksha.

Mr. Shen escaped death narrowly. His assassins escaped the law completely. The rice magnate was wounded in the arm, which was fractured by the missile.

Reports charging that Mr. Shen was one of the six men interrogated and warned by the Shanghai Municipal Police on Thursday for violating the terms of the joint anti-manipulation proclamation of the two foreign municipalities were denied yesterday. The motive for the attack, however, was unknown.

Rice riots yesterday were becoming too numerous for the police to keep an immediate, exact record. First known riot and the largest up to 4 p.m. occurred at 9 a.m. at 1397 Ferry Road, where 12 men were arrested. Much of the stolen grain was recovered.

The rioters struck over a wide area. Rice hongs on Kaifeng, Chengtu, Taku, Shanhaikwan, Burkill, Robinson, Carter, Ichang and Kiaochow Roads were victimized in the International Settlement. In one case the rioters got away with $400 worth of rice which they loaded on rickshas.

Losses Terrific

Outstanding in most of the riots was the fact that the unruly crowds almost invariably demanded 20 cents' worth of grain which was refused by shops selling for a minimum of $1.

In two instances, however, police squads which rushed to the scene ordered the shops to sell the crowds 20 cents' worth.

Meanwhile, a fairly accurate report of rioters' activities on Friday shows that 36 hongs were raided, 92 men and women arrested, and 1,300 piculs of rice, valued at approximately $60,000, were stolen in the course of the riots.

Stores which lost more than 100 piculs, worth approximately $4,500, each were the Tung Hai Rice Shop on Edinburgh Road, the Wei Shing Rice Shop on Jessfield Road, the Chien Zung and Tuh Zung Rice Shops on Great Western Road, the San Tai Rice Shop on Robison Road, and the Vai Tai Rice Shop on Route des Soeurs.

Danish girls who believe in old customs kiss their hands on hearing the first cuckoo of the year.

So popular is horseback riding in England that the country has more than 2000 riding academies today, compared to 400 less than five years ago.

《字林西报》
1939年

五十人在此间二十四起米骚乱中被捕

谷物价值：四万美元
被劫掠者盗走，骚乱浪潮持续

仅昨日早上九时至午夜之间，就发生了二十四起米骚乱，其中包括三起发生在法租界（Frenchtown）的案件。期间被盗大米八百余石，价值超过四万美元，另有五十余人被捕。

尽管警方竭尽全力对米行提供充分保护，并在数起事件中平息了骚乱——警察小队迫使人群在店外排成有序的队伍——然而，要在每一家米店门口增派警卫在体力上是不可能的；虽然已对位于本市较偏僻地区的米行加强了警力保护，但昨日的骚乱仍有增无减。

骚乱达到顶峰

上午十时，骚乱达到顶峰。六十三岁的富商沈藏文（Shen Zang-ven，音译）先生在其位于浙江路145号的办事处经营米业，当他乘坐私人黄包车沿福州路行驶时，两名男子向他开枪，致其手臂受伤。

沈先生险些丧命。刺客完全逃脱了法律制裁。这位米业大亨手臂受伤，子弹导致骨折。

昨日有人否认了有关沈先生是周四因违反两外国租界联合发布的反操纵公告而受到上海公共租界工部局警务处讯问和警告的六人之一的指控。不过，袭击动机尚不清楚。

昨日的米骚乱次数过多，警方无法立即进行精确记录。已知的第一起骚乱，也是截至下午四时规模最大的一起，发生于上午九时的斐伦路（Ferry Road）1397号，当时有十二人被捕。大部分被盗粮食已被追回。

暴徒在广大区域作案。公共租界内开封路、成都路、大沽路、山海关路、伯基尔路（Burkill Road）、罗宾逊路（Robinson Road）、卡特路（Carter Road）、宜昌路和胶州路的米行均遭受害。在其中一起案件中，暴徒将价值四百美元的大米装上黄包车后逃离。

损失惨重

大多数骚乱中一个显著的事实是，无序的人群几乎总是要求购买价值二十美分的粮食，而商店拒绝以低于一美元的最低售价出售。

然而，在两起案件中，赶至现场的警察小队命令商店向人群出售价值二十美分的粮食。

与此同时，一份关于周五暴徒活动的相当准确的报告显示，在骚乱过程中，三十六家米行遭到抢劫，九十二名男女被捕，一千三百石大米被盗，价值约六万美元。

每家损失超过一百石（价值约四千五百美元）的商店包括：爱丁堡路（Edinburgh Road）的东海米店、极司菲尔路（Jessfield Road）的伟兴米店、大西路（Great Western Road）的建中和独中米店、罗宾逊路（Robison Road）的三泰米店，以及姐妹会路（Route des Soeurs）的伟泰米店。

相信古老习俗的丹麦女孩在听到当年的第一声布谷鸟叫时会亲吻自己的手。

骑马在英国如此受欢迎，以至于该国如今拥有两千多所骑术学校，而五年前还只有四百所。

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS.

1937

Racketeers Seen
Behind Rioting

Intimidators and Loafers
Arrested as New Wave of
Rice Raids Sweeps City

In the course of another day marked by mob raids on dozens of rice shops, the Settlement Police yesterday arrested a number of Chinese racketeers who have been instigating many of the disturbances and also took into custody scores of loafers who were active in the raids and some of whom suffered broken pates as a result of baton charges. Most rice shops in the Settlement and the French Concession closed their doors at 5 p.m.. The price of the grain declined only $1 per picul yesterday, and the cheap supplies promised by the Japanese army last Tuesday did not materialize. There were no reports of rice riots in the Eastern district.

Eight calls to rice shops were answered by police at the Bubbling Well Station, who broke up the disturbances and recovered some of the stolen grain. They arrested nine troublemakers, but more important was the rounding-up of racketeers in the district who had been mulcting shop owners under threat of causing the establishments to be wrecked. Here, as elsewhere, an organized racket was indicated. In some instances the owners paid rather than risk a visit by the mob.

The biggest raid on rice in the Bubbling Well district occurred at 32 Annam Road, where seventy piculs of rice and thirty bags of flour were stolen. The police recovered only a small part of the loot but arrested five of the looters. Thirty piculs were stolen at 283 Hart Road, where four men were arrested.

13 Raids in Five Hours

The congested Sinza district, which has a large number of rice shops, experienced nineteen riots during the day. Twelve Chinese, mostly of the loafer type, were arrested. Two of the rioters were treated in hospital for broken heads incurred during the disturbances. All thirteen raids took place within five hours, between 11.15 a.m. and 4.15 p.m.

In other districts the attacks started earlier in the day. A large-scale disturbance took place in the Pootoo Road district at 9 o'clock when a mob of several hundred looted 1397 Ferry Road. The police arrested 21 men and women and recovered most of the stolen rice. The Chengtu Road district had many raids and other disturbances were quelled in the West Hongkew, Gordon Road and Louza areas. Three looters with broken pates were sent to the Police Hospital from 66 Taku Road after an attack.

The Settlement Police and the French Concession Police both responded to a call to 866 Avenue Haig, where a shop was being looted.

Woman Trampled by Mob

It was ascertained yesterday that a Chinese woman died as a result of being trampled by a mob stampeding through a narrow lane in one of Friday evening's tumults in the western district. These disturbances, which took place in rapid succession at a number of shops in the highly-populated areas, were likewise attributed chiefly to the work of Chinese racket leaders and their loafer and opium-addict henchmen.

The retail price of rice in Shanghai yesterday was from $39 to $42 per picul for the best grade or "kan mee," and $34 to $35 for "see mee." This represented a reduction of $1 per picul since Friday. Saigon rice was being sold for about the same price as the domestic grain.

Three Strikes Settled

In the field of labour some improvement was achieved when three strikes were ended. The establishments in which work was resumed were the China Soap Co., British, Yangtszepoo; the Ewo Cold Storage Co., British, Yangtszepoo; and the China Native Products Co., Nanking Road, Chinese.

At a meeting held yesterday afternoon, the executives of the Shanghai Rice and Bean Dealers Association decided further to reduce the prices of their goods. The first grade rice was fixed at $40 as compared with $45 last week, and the "see mee" at $33, showing also five dollars' decrease. While thus trying to alleviate the situation by reducing prices, members of the association petitioned the authorities for full protection so that they could do business today.

Market Closed

The Shanghai Rice Market was closed yesterday because of the many raids no shops. Realizing that the situation was becoming extremely serious the executives of the association hurriedly held a conference in the afternoon. Although the market could not be opened yesterday it was learned last night that it would be opened today. A Chinese evening report stated that the closing of the market was considered by some quarters as a "quiet protest" against the proclamation issued by the authorities against rice profiteers.

The police of the French Concession dealt with seven rice riots yesterday and arrested over a dozen looters and instigators.

《字林西报》。

1937年

暴乱背后现流氓身影

随着新一波抢米风潮席卷全市，恐吓者与游民被捕

在又一天发生数十家米店遭暴徒抢劫的事件中，公共租界警务处于昨日逮捕了一批一直煽动诸多骚乱的中国流氓分子，并拘留了数十名积极参与抢劫的游民，其中一些人因警棍驱散而头部受伤。公共租界和法租界的大多数米店于下午5时关门。昨日米价每石仅下跌1元，日军上周二承诺提供的廉价大米并未兑现。东区未收到发生米骚乱的报告。

静安寺捕房警方出警处理了八起针对米店的报警，平息了骚乱并追回部分被窃大米。他们逮捕了九名滋事者，但更重要的是在该区 roundup（围捕）了一直以毁坏店铺相威胁、向店主勒索钱财的流氓。在此处及其他地方，均显示出有组织的勒索活动迹象。在某些情况下，店主为避免暴徒光顾而选择付款。

静安寺区最大规模的抢米事件发生在安南路32号，七十石大米和三十袋面粉被盗。警方仅追回少量赃物，但逮捕了五名抢劫者。哈特路283号被盗三十石大米，四人被捕。

五小时内发生十三起抢劫

拥有众多米店的拥挤新闸区，当天发生了十九起骚乱。十二名中国人被捕，大多属于游民类型。两名骚乱者因在骚乱中头部受伤而在医院接受治疗。所有十三起抢劫均发生在上午11时15分至下午4时15分这五个小时内。

在其他区域，袭击发生得更早。上午9时，普陀路地区发生大规模骚乱，数百名暴徒洗劫了斐伦路1397号。警方逮捕了21名男女，并追回了大部分被盗大米。成都路地区发生多起抢劫，西虹口、戈登路和老闸地区的其他骚乱也被平息。大沽路66号遇袭后，三名头部受伤的抢劫者被送往警务处医院。

公共租界警务处和法租界警务处均响应了对海格路866号的报警，当时该店正遭抢劫。

女子被暴徒踩踏致死

经查明，一名中国妇女在周五晚间西区的一场骚乱中，因被穿过狭窄弄堂的惊慌奔逃的暴徒踩踏而死亡。这些在人口稠密地区的多家店铺接连迅速发生的骚乱，同样主要归咎于中国流氓头目及其游民和鸦片瘾者帮凶所为。

昨日上海大米零售价格，上等米或“粳米”为每石39至42元，“籼米”为34至35元。这表示自周五以来每石下跌1元。西贡米的售价与国产米大致相同。

三起罢工得以解决

劳工领域取得了一些进展，三起罢工结束。恢复工作的机构包括：位于杨树浦英商区的中国肥皂公司（China Soap Co.）、位于杨树浦英商区的怡和冷藏公司（Ewo Cold Storage Co.）以及位于南京路华商区的中国国货公司（China Native Products Co.）。

在昨日下午举行的会议上，上海米豆业同业公会执行委员决定进一步降低商品价格。一等米定价为40元，而上周为45元；“籼米”定价为33元，也下降了5元。在试图通过降价缓解局势的同时，公会成员向当局请愿，要求提供全面保护，以便他们今日能够营业。

市场关闭

由于多家店铺遭抢劫，上海米市昨日关闭。鉴于局势变得极其严重，公会执行委员于下午紧急召开会议。虽然昨日市场未能开市，但昨晚获悉今日将开市。一份中文晚报称，某些方面将市场关闭视为对当局发布的打击米商囤积居奇公告的一种“无声抗议”。

法租界警方昨日处理了七起米骚乱，逮捕了十余名抢劫者和煽动者。

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS
DEC 1. 7 1939
Chengtu Road Rice
Disturbance
Police Called Out to
Quell Riot; Arrest Three
Principal Offenders
Typical of most of the rice riots,
the one which broke out in the San
Mow Rice Shop in Chengtu Road
near Taku Road yesterday morning
and which was viewed by a repre-
sentative of the "North-China Daily
News" was started by only a few
poor people whose offers to buy 20
or 30 cents worth of rice were turn-
ed down. Soon more poor men
gathered to see what was happening
and heated arguments which ensued
attracted more pedestrians and sym-
pathizers who began to shout com-
plaints.
Shop assistants tried to hurriedly
shut the door shortly before 11 a.m.
The crowd was then eight or nine
persons deep. Two constables hope-
lessly tried to pacify the rioters.
Before the angry shop assistants
could close the door entirely the
crowd became larger and began
storming the shop by forming human
ladders.
The poorer people who usually are
much afraid of the police paid no
heed to the latter's words, elbowed
for better positions in the crowd,
and began a mad stampede for the
door which could not be closed.
Many succeeded in entering the shop
by climbing over their fellows, and
stole flour.
Shops Close Doors
Rice and beans placed in baskets
near the door as sample goods were
spilled and trodden on. Part of the
pavement and the dark winter police
uniforms were covered with white
flour. The battle was concluded
within about 20 minutes, leaving in
its wake many discarded shoes and
spilled rice and flour. Three rioters
were taken to Chengtu Road Police
Station in a van. Rice shops in
other streets also closed their doors
leaving small openings through
which to transact business.
In a way the shop assistants could
hardly be blamed for the trouble
for they said that they had no
measures which could hold only 20
or 30 cents' worth of rice. Judging
from complaints made by the poor
yesterday it would appear that they
misinterpreted the proclamation
issued by the Settlement authorities
warning rice profiteers that no
sanctuary would be given them.
It would also seem that they riot
thinking that the smaller retailers
are the profiteers.

《字林西报》
1939年12月7日
成都路米骚动
警方出动平息暴乱；逮捕三名主要肇事者

昨日早晨发生在靠近大沽路的成都路三茂米店的米骚动，与大多数米骚动一样，据《字林西报》一名代表观察，该事件仅由几名穷人发起，他们提出购买价值20或30美分的米遭拒。随后更多穷人聚集围观事态发展， ensuing 的激烈争吵吸引了更多行人和同情者，他们开始高声抱怨。

上午11点前不久，店员试图匆忙关闭店门。当时人群已有八九层之厚。两名巡捕徒劳地试图安抚暴乱者。在愤怒的店员完全关上店门之前，人群规模扩大，并开始通过搭人梯的方式冲击店铺。

那些通常非常害怕警察的穷人对警察的喊话置若罔闻，在人群中推搡以占据更有利的位置，并开始疯狂冲向那扇无法关上的大门。许多人成功爬过同伴身体进入店内，并偷窃面粉。

店铺关门

放在门口篮子里作为样品的米和豆子被泼洒并遭践踏。部分人行道以及深色的冬季警服上覆盖着白色面粉。这场冲突在约20分钟内结束，现场留下许多丢弃的鞋子以及泼洒的米和面粉。三名暴乱者被警车带往成都路巡捕房。其他街道的米店也关闭了店门，仅留小口进行交易。

从某种程度来说，店员们对于引发麻烦几乎无可指责，因为他们表示，店里没有能够仅称量价值20或30美分米的措施。根据昨日穷人的投诉来看，他们似乎误解了租界当局发布的公告，该公告警告囤积居奇的米商将不再受到庇护。此外，他们似乎误以为小零售商就是囤积居奇者。

DEC 16 1933
27810
8009/5(0)
11 2 7

Hungry And Infuriated No. 5.
Mobs Stage Wholesale
Rice Riots Over City

21 Rice Hongs Looted During Day In Settlement;
Police Busy Dispersing Mobs, Recovering
Stolen Rice And Making Arrests

WARNING SHOTS FIRED INTO AIR BY
POLICE TO FRIGHTEN CROWDS

Wholesale rice riots broke out all over the Shanghai International Settlement, especially along the Outside Roads, early yesterday afternoon. Hungry and infuriated mobs attacked rice shops, creating a pandemonium all over the city and necessitating the turn out of squads of police to clear the unruly crowds.

In two instances warning shots had to be fired by the police into the air to scare away the angry mobs. Well over 60 arrests were made by officers of the different police stations in whose districts the riots occurred. Most of the riots were staged in the Bubbling Well district, especially along Brenan, Edinburgh and Yu Yuen Roads.

The frightened rice shop proprietors and assistants put up their shutters and closed their shops, but in a number of cases the mobs broke down the doors and on getting inside the stores started looting as much rice as they possibly could. Large quantities of rice were stolen from the various hongs, in some cases well over 30 or even 50 piculs being carried away prior to arrival of squads of police.

Although no definite proof was available last night, it was generally believed that the majority of the riots, especially those that were staged along Edinburgh, Brenan and Bubbling Well Roads, early yesterday afternoon were organized. The riots in the area were staged within the space of two hours, between 2.30 and 4.40 p.m. Seven arrests were made at the five riots by officers of the Bubbling Well Police Station, who rushed from the scene of one riot to another.

Shots Fired

On being unable to halt a large mob from looting a rice hong at 301 Seymour Road at about 3 o'clock yesterday afternoon, a lone Chinese constable of the Shanghai Municipal Police, fired two shots into the air in order to frighten the crowd away or at least to cool their ardour. The mob halted for a minute, but then with a cry rushed the shop, broke down the door and commenced looting. A call for assistance was put through to the Bubbling Well Police Station and a party immediately turned out, clearing the remains of the crowd away.

Several shots were reported to have been fired into the air at about 5.20 p.m. during the mob attack staged on a rice shop at the corner of Edinburgh and Yu Yuen Roads. A check-up among the officers of the S.M.P., who turned out to the scene revealed that no shots were fired by them. It was believed that the warning shots were fired by City Government policemen, but this could not be checked last night.

While in some cases the attacks on hongs were organized by hooligans, in other cases there was a spontaneous flare-up when purchasers were not able to obtain the staple product at prices to meet their pockets. The customers would start arguing with the shop assistants, crowds would gather around the shop, become infuriated and then an attack on the shop and looting would follow.

Special Guards

Despite the fact that most of the rice hongs had closed up early in the afternoon and are likely to keep their premises padlocked to-day, special police guards have been placed at all rice shops all over the city to prevent any further mob-attacks.

Officers of Bubbling Well, Gordon Road, Pootoo Road and Sinza Police Stations were kept busy throughout the day turning out to rice riots, make arrests and inquiring into the various cases.

The first riot of the day occurred at 7.15 a.m. when a large crowd attacked a rice hong at 76 Singapore Road and stole 20 piculs of rice. A party of police from Pootoo Road Police Station responded to the call and arrested three men and women and recovered a quantity of the stolen rice.

In the afternoon the riots came in such rapid order that it was almost impossible to keep check on them, police moving from one scene to another with hardly time to return to the station.

In French Concession

Only one rice riot was staged in the French Concession during the course of the day. The rice hong located at No. 414 Rue Tenant de La Tour was raided by a large crowd of Chinese at 4.30 p.m., and two piculs of rice were stolen. Promptly after the theft the mob dispersed and scattered. No shots were fired by the police and no arrests made.

Special precautions are being taken by the French Concession authorities. A party will patrol in front of rice shops in the Concession to-day in an attempt to avoid the gathering of mobs and raids of rice shops. It is understood that plans have been made for police riot vans or patrols in armoured cars to pass rice shops within periods of 15 minutes.

No rice riots were reported to have taken place yesterday within the Settlement or Concession after 6.50 p.m. The rice hongs in general close down after 5 o'clock.

Widespread rumours that a mass rice riot was going to be staged during the afternoon caused almost all stores in the French Concession to close up for business shortly after 4 o'clock.

Riots were staged at the following hongs:

Three riots between 11 a.m. and 3 p.m. in the Bubbling Well district.
2.30 p.m.—Lane 391, House 1,107 Haiphong Road. 17 arrests.
3.10 p.m.—512 Tatung Road. Several arrests.
3.50 p.m.—820 Avenue Road. Two arrests.
3.00 p.m.—301 Seymour Road.
4.10 p.m.—372 Medhurst Road.
2.30 to 4.40 p.m.—323 Brenan Road, 502 Brenan, 37 Brenan Road, 1954 Bubbling Well Road, 623 Edinburgh Road. Seven arrests.
3.51 p.m.—959 Ferry Road. One arrest.
4.15 p.m.—522 Wuting Road. Eight arrests.
4.50 p.m.—932-4 Sinza Road.
4.50 p.m.—886 Sinza Road.
5.00 p.m.—1309 Penang Road. Six arrests.
5.20 p.m.—401 Robison Road. Twelve arrests.
6.50 p.m.—301 Seymour Road. (Second attack).

（批：Liu. C 16/12）

1933年12月16日

饥愤交加的暴民（五）。
全城爆发大规模
米骚乱

租界内21家米行在日间遭劫掠；
警方忙于驱散暴民、追回被盗大米并实施逮捕

警方为震慑人群向空中鸣枪示警

昨天下午早些时候，上海公共租界各地，尤其是外滩沿线道路，爆发了大规模米骚乱。饥饿且愤怒的暴民袭击米店，导致全城陷入一片混乱，迫使警方出动小队以驱散这些不法人群。

在两起事件中，警方不得不向空中鸣枪示警，以吓退愤怒的暴民。各辖区发生骚乱的警察局警官共实施了超过60次逮捕。大多数骚乱发生在静安寺区，尤其是沿贝勒路（Brenan Road）、爱丁堡路（Edinburgh Road）和愚园路（Yu Yuen Road）一带。

受惊的米店店主和店员放下门板，关闭店铺，但在多起案件中，暴民砸开大门，进入店内后开始尽可能多地抢掠大米。各家米行被盗走大量大米，在某些情况下，在警察小队抵达之前，被抢走的大米多达30甚至50担以上。

虽然昨晚尚无确凿证据，但人们普遍认为，昨天下午早些时候发生的大多数骚乱，特别是沿爱丁堡路、贝勒路和静安寺路（Bubbling Well Road）发生的骚乱，是有组织的。该区域的骚乱发生在下午2点30分至4点40分这两个小时内。静安寺捕房的警官从一处骚乱现场赶往另一处，在五起骚乱中实施了七次逮捕。

鸣枪

昨天下午3点左右，在上海西摩路（Seymour Road）301号，一名上海公共租界工部局警务处的华籍巡警因无法阻止一大群暴民抢劫一家米行，遂向空中连开两枪，以期吓退人群或至少平息其狂热情绪。暴民停顿了一分钟，但随后呼喊着冲向店铺，砸开大门并开始抢掠。随即向静安寺捕房发出求援呼叫，一队警力立即出动，驱散了剩余的人群。

据报道，下午5点20分左右，在爱丁堡路与愚园路转角处的一家米店遭受暴民袭击期间，曾向空中发射数发子弹。经核查赶赴现场的工部局警务处警官，发现他们并未开枪。据信示警枪声由市政府警察发射，但昨晚未能对此进行核实。

虽然在某些情况下，对米行的袭击是由流氓地痞组织的，但在其他情况下，当购买者无法以承受得起的价格买到这种主食时，也会自发爆发冲突。顾客开始与店员争吵，人群聚集在店铺周围，变得愤怒，随后便发生袭击店铺和抢掠行为。

特别警卫

尽管大多数米行已在下午早些时候关门，并且今天可能会将场所上锁，但全市所有米店均已部署特别警察警卫，以防止进一步的暴民袭击。

静安寺、戈登路（Gordon Road）、普陀路（Pootoo Road）和新闸（Sinza）捕房的警官整天忙于应对米骚乱、实施逮捕以及调查各类案件。

当天的第一起骚乱发生在上午7点15分，当时一大群人袭击了新加坡路（Singapore Road）76号的一家米行，偷走了20担大米。普陀路捕房的一队警察响应呼叫，逮捕了三名男女，并追回了一定数量的被盗大米。

下午，骚乱接踵而至，几乎无法逐一记录，警察从一个现场赶往下一个现场，几乎没有时间返回警局。

在法租界

当天法租界内仅发生了一起米骚乱。下午4点30分，一大群中国人洗劫了位于谭维路（Rue Tenant de La Tour）414号的一家米行，偷走了两担大米。盗窃发生后，暴民迅速解散并四散而去。警方未开枪，也未实施逮捕。

法租界当局正在采取特别预防措施。今天将有一队警力在租界内的米店前巡逻，试图避免暴民聚集和对米店的突袭。据悉，已制定计划，安排防暴警车或装甲车巡逻队每隔15分钟经过米店一次。

据报道，晚上6点50分之后，租界或法租界内未再发生米骚乱。米行通常在下午5点后关门。

关于下午将爆发大规模米骚乱的广泛谣言，导致法租界内几乎所有商店在下午4点后不久便停止营业。

以下米行发生了骚乱：

静安寺区在上午11点至下午3点之间发生三起骚乱。
下午2点30分——海防路（Haiphong Road）1107号，391弄。17人被捕。
下午3点10分——大通路（Tatung Road）512号。数人被捕。
下午3点50分——爱文义路（Avenue Road）820号。两人被捕。
下午3点00分——西摩路301号。
下午4点10分——麦赫斯特路（Medhurst Road）372号。
下午2点30分至4点40分——贝勒路323号、贝勒路502号、贝勒路37号、静安寺路1954号、爱丁堡路623号。七人被捕。
下午3点51分——斐伦路（Ferry Road）959号。一人被捕。
下午4点15分——吴淞路（Wuting Road）522号。八人被捕。
下午4点50分——新闸路932-4号。
下午4点50分——新闸路886号。
下午5点00分——槟榔路（Penang Road）1309号。六人被捕。
下午5点20分——罗宾森路（Robison Road）401号。十二人被捕。
下午6点50分——西摩路301号。（第二次袭击）。

（批注：Liu. C 16/12）
