SHANGHAI TIMES.
DEC 15 1939
Rice Riot Is
Staged By An
Irate Crowd
Police Are Called Out
To Disperse Crowd
In Hart Rd. Raid
FOUR CHINESE TO BE
CHARGED IN COURT
A crowd of about 100 hungry
Chinese, among them a certain
amount of the criminal element,
staged a rice riot on Hart
Road, in the midst of the poor
man's district, yesterday after-
noon. The crowd raided a rice
shop at 1,460 Hart Road at
about 5.30 p.m., managing to
steal over 40 bags of rice before
a party of police from Pootoo
Road Police Station arrived on
the scene and scattered the
rioters.
Pandemonium reigned for a
while as infuriated men and
shrieking women scrambled to lay
their hands on as much rice as
they could carry away. The shop
assistants fought tooth and nail,
but were overpowered. A couple
of policemen rushed to the scene,
but could do nothing to stop the
rush of about 100 hungry people.
A call for assistance was put
through to the Pootoo Road Police
Station and a party of police,
under Inspector Watson, responded
immediately, clearing the crowd a
few minutes after they came on
the scene and detaining seven
men. After investigation, four of
the men were placed under arrest
and will be charged in the First
Special District Court this morn-
ing. It was estimated that over
$1,500 of rice was stolen and
scattered over the street during
the riot.
After the riot, a guard was left
at the victimized hong, while
other rice stores in the city are
also being given special protection.
Drop In Price
The local rice market remained
very quiet yesterday, with the
price of the first quality of the
staple dropping to $43 per picul.
as compared with $45 on Wednes-
day. Purchasers, both local and
outport, were reluctant to buy at
yesterday's prices, expecting a
sharp drop within the not too dis-
tant future.
Although the best quality rice
was quoted at $43 in the official
market, many retail stores were
offering the same quality at as low
as $40 per picul. The shopkeepers
explained that they had bought
their stocks at a time when the
prices were far below the present
level and that they wished to pass
on part of their profits to their
customers.
It was reported yesterday that
over 10,000 bags of foreign rice
arrived in Shanghai yesterday and
that about 1,100 bags of domestic
rice was brought in by rail and
junk.
（批：80299/5(0)-2  2  39）

四名华人将被
起诉至法庭
昨日下午，在贫民区中心的赫德路（Hart Road），约100名饥饿的华人（其中包含一定数量的犯罪分子）制造了一起米骚乱。下午5时30分左右，这群人洗劫了赫德路1460号的一家米店，在普陀路警察局的警员赶到现场并驱散暴徒之前，他们设法偷走了40多袋大米。
现场一度陷入混乱，愤怒的男子和尖叫的妇女争先恐后地抢夺尽可能多的大米。店员们奋力抵抗，但被制服。几名警察迅速赶至现场，但无法阻止约100名饥民的冲击。
随后向普陀路警察局发出求援呼叫，由沃森（Watson）巡官率领的一队警员立即响应，在抵达现场几分钟后驱散了人群，并拘留了七名男子。经调查，其中四人被逮捕，将于今晨在第一特区法院被起诉。据估计，骚乱期间被盗并散落在街道上的大米价值超过1,500元。
骚乱过后，受害的商号留下了守卫人员，同时市内其他米店也获得了特别保护。
价格下跌
昨日本地米市保持非常平静，上等主粮米的价格降至每担43元，而周三为45元。本地及外埠买家均不愿按昨日的价格购买，预期在不久的将来价格会大幅下跌。
尽管官方市场上等米的报价为43元，但许多零售店以低至每担40元的价格出售同等质量的米。店主解释说，他们的库存是在价格远低于目前水平时购入的，他们希望将部分利润让利给顾客。
据昨日报道，昨天有超过10,000袋洋米运抵上海，另有约1,100袋国米通过铁路和木船运入。

NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS.

DEC 15 1939

Rice Rioting Breaks
Out in Hart Road

Mob of 100 Force Way Into
Shop; Six Men Arrested

With the rice situation still at the
critical stage an ugly riot flared out
in Hart Road at 5.35 p.m. yesterday
when a howling mob of over 100 men
forced their way into a rice shop at
1789 Hart Road and in a desperate,
brutal scramble for the precious
foodstuff made off with over $1,500
worth of rice.
A telephone call to Pootoo Road
police station sent a squad of police
racing to the scene to disperse the
mob. Six men were arrested and
will face the First Special District
Court this morning. No one was
hurt during the incident and the
police managed to clear the street
with little difficulty.

百名暴徒强行闯入店铺；六人被捕

鉴于米粮局势仍处于危急阶段，昨日下午5时35分，赫德路爆发了一起恶劣的骚乱。当时，一百多名男子组成的咆哮暴徒强行闯入赫德路1789号的一家米店，在疯狂而野蛮地争抢这种珍贵食品后，携价值超过1,500元的米粮逃离现场。

一通打往普陀路警察局的电话促使一队警察迅速赶赴现场驱散暴徒。六名男子被捕，将于今晨在第一特区法院受审。事件期间无人受伤，警方毫不费力地疏通了街道。

A party of Police under the Inspt. i/ch, including C.D.C. 100 and the undersigned, immediately attended the scene and dispersed a crowd of approximately 100 male and female Chinese from the footpath outside the above shop.
Enquiries elicited that at 10.30 a.m. a small boy Tsu Wei Kyah (朱維嘉), aged 14, residing 19 Ching Kah Ong off Sinza Road O.O.L. purchased rice to the value of $1.00 from a shop assistant named Wo Tsoong Zien (何仲銓), employed in the Doong Tan Rice Shop.
On receiving the rice the boy complained to the shop-assistant Wo Tsoong Zien that the amount of rice given him for $1.00 was insufficient.
The shop-assistant became angry with the boy and slapped his face. The boy thereupon returned to his home with the rice he had purchased and informed his father Tsu Kung Pao (朱根宝) of his trouble at the rice shop.
The father Tsu Kung Pao accompanied his son to the rice shop where he demanded that the shop-assistant Wo Tsoong Zien explain why he had slapped his son and he also demanded the assistant weigh the rice, purchased by his son, in his presence.

8月24日，浦东有九家米店遭到暴民洗劫，暴民主要由妇女和未成年人组成。涉事店铺遭受的损失从十担至三十担大米不等，受害店铺如下：

8月24日上午11时，浦东十八间 (Shih Pah Ken) 的三家米店遭到暴民洗劫，一队上海市政府警察赶到并成功逮捕了约二十名抢劫者。经向店主查明除大米外未失窃其他物品后，对抢劫者予以警告并释放。

在此类事件发生后，浦东警察局通知其他米店关门，以防备暴民的进一步袭击。

然而，驻浦东的日本海军当局对米粮状况持漠不关心的态度，且在骚乱之后，日本海军当局禁止其人员离开在浦东的驻地，推测是为了避免受到干扰。

Subject (in full) Looting of Rice Shops in Nantao.

Made by D.I. Pan Lien Pih Forwarded by C. Gauson S.I

On August 22, 1939, a further case of rice
shop being looted occurred in Nantao. At 7 a.m. that
day, about 30 loafers and destitute persons entered a
rice shop called Kiu Dah (久大) at 52 Tsing Loong
Jao, Sih Ka Pang, Nantao, and looted a total of five
"zars" of rice. A party of police arrived on the
scene but the intruders had already dispersed.

There are approximately sixty rice shops
situated in the City and Nantao, and in consequence
of the looting which occurred on August 21 and 22,
some twenty of them suspended business on August 22.

Made by. D.I. Pan Lien Pih Forwarded by. C. Gayford. S.S.
The following cases of rice shops
being looted are reported to have occurred
in the City on August 21, 1939 :-
At 9 a.m., about 30 loafers and coolies
forced an entry into the Tuh Zung Rice Shop
(德盛), 126 Siao Pootoo Chiao, Tung
Ka Doo, Nantao, and commenced looting the rice
stock stored in the shop. Six piculs of
rice were taken away by these people before
the arrival of the Japanese Military and the
Chinese Police and no arrests were made.
At 11 a.m., some forty persons con-
sisting of loafers and destitute persons broke
into the Zai Dah (穗大) Rice Shop, 65
Tah Ching Road, in the Refugee Zone, City, and
looted a total of four piculs of rice. The
Police arrived on the scene but no arrests were
made.
It is learned that the price for
ordinary rice in the City is $31.00 per "zar"
and that transportation of rice into the City
has been prohibited by the Japanese Military
authorities functioning in the Western District
of Shanghai, at Siking and also Tse Pao.

Sir,
At 8.30 p.m. 23/8/39 a telephone message was received from the Heng Dah (恆大) Rice Shop, 225 Yates Road stating a mob were attempting to loot the shop. a party of Police consisting of S.I. Moffat, D.S.I. Black, D.S.I. Yang, P.C.S. 66 and uniform Police proceeded to the scene but no untoward offence was observed, beyond a crowd collected in the vicinity.

Enquiries from the shop-master Zau Boh Dau (起福道) show that as the shop was closing for business at 8.30 p.m. 23/8/39 a large number of customers demanded service and this frightened the shop-master who put up the shutters and telephoned the station.

No rice was looted and no damage done. Obviously a case of undue alarm on the part of the shop-master.

Police on duty warned to pay special attention to the shop.

Remarks
(Any outstanding or peculiar feature to be
commented on by investigating officer).

At 8.15 p.m. 23-8-39, a telephone message was
received at Yulin Road Station to the effect that a
riot was in progress at the Zung Teh Daung (存德堂)
Medicine Shop, 502, Ward Road.

In response to this message a party of police
attended the scene, and dispersed a crowd of persons
who had gathered outside the premises.

Enquiries ascertained that a rumour had been
circulated amongst residents in the vicinity of the
Zung Teh Daung Medicine Shop to the effect that some
six hundred sacks of rice had been stored in the shop
for safe-keeping by one named Woo Paung Vung (胡榜文),
the proprietor of the Shanghai (上海) Rice Shop,
490 Ward Road.

The party of Police looked over the premises,
and found that no rice whatever was stored therein,
the rumour being obviously unfounded.

When the party of Police returned to the station
Hav. 470 and S.P.C. 376 were detailed for duty at
the scene, in order to prevent further disturbances.

At 9 p.m. 23-8-1939, P.S. 334 Kay telephoned the
station to the effect that the crowd had again as-
sembled and were preparing to attack the shop.

A party of Police, with Inspector Brownrigg,
Officer i/c, responded to the call, and upon arrival
found that P.S. Kay and the two Sikh officers had
detained three male Chinese, named:-

(1) Lee Yung Sung (李雲生) 36, Zaushing,
M/coolie, 50 Yue Wha Faung, Ward Road.

(2) Zung Ah Kung (陳阿根) 24, Wusih,
M/coolie, 68 Yue Wha Faung, Ward Road.

备注
（任何显著或特殊特征，由调查警官予以评注）。

1939年8月23日晚8时15分，榆林路捕房接到一通电话消息，称华德路502号存德堂（Zung Teh Daung）药店正在发生骚乱。

警方随即派员赶赴现场，驱散了聚集在该处所外的人群。

经查询得知，在存德堂药店附近居民中流传着一则谣言，称华德路490号上海（Shanghai）米店店主胡榜文（Woo Paung Vung）已将约六百袋大米存入该店保管。

警员对该处所进行了检查，发现店内并未储存任何大米，该谣言显然毫无根据。

警队返回捕房后，指派警长第470号及锡克警曹第376号前往现场执勤，以防止进一步滋扰。

1939年8月23日晚9时，警司第334号凯（Kay）致电捕房，称人群再次聚集，并正准备袭击该商店。

由布朗里格（Brownrigg）巡官率领的一队警员响应呼叫赶赴现场，抵达后发现凯警司及两名锡克警员已拘留三名华籍男子，姓名如下：

(1) 李雲生，36岁，浙江绍兴人，男/苦力，住华德路月华坊50号。

(2) 陳阿根（Zung Ah Kung），24岁，江苏无锡人，男/苦力，住华德路月华坊68号。

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

The eight accused appeared before the S.S.D. Court
on the a.m. of 21/8/39 when the 1st to the 7th accused
were ordered remanded until the 30/8/39, the 8th accused
was ordered detained until that date.

During the period of detention the 8th accused
has been frequently interrogated by detectives but it
has proven impossible to connect him in any way with
this offence and upon his appearance before the S.S.D.
Court on the a.m. of 30/8/39 his release will be request-
ed and the 'Writ of Detention' in respect of him will
be withdrawn.

The 1st to the 7th accused have been further
interrogated but all deny having any knowledge of other
offences and it has proven impossible to connect them
with any other offences, although each of them was
arrested in possession of stolen property in connection
with the offence that forms the subject of this report.

The eight accused will again appear before the
S.S.D. Court on the a.m. of 30/8/39 when, as mentioned

Remarks
(Any outstanding or peculiar feature to be
commented on by investigating officer).

At. 8.05 p.m. 20/8/39 a telephone message was
received at this station from the Yi Yue Shing
(裕源新) Rice and Flour Shop 69 Changping Road, to
the effect that a large crowd had gathered outside
the shop and that they were breaking down the doors.
C.D.C. 242, C.P.C. 2734 and the undersigned
immediately attended and found that a mob numbering
approximately 500 persons had stormed the shop in
question and had wrenched the iron grilles from the
front and side of the shop and forced open the
wooden shutters and were engaged in
looting bags of flour from the shop.
The police party immediately set upon the
mob and with the assistance of C.D.S. 202 and one
of his agents named Sung Koh Tsung (宋國忠) (C.D.
S. 202 was off duty and together with his agent was
attracted to the scene by the sight of the crowd),
succeeded in dispersing the mob.
After dispersing the main body of the mob the
station was informed of the situation and a further
party under S/I Glanville attended the scene.
Whilst dispersing the mob the first four
accused, (1) Yung Zang Foh (尹長福), (2) Wong Sau
Yung (王秀英), (3) Kyung Zang Kung (慶長根) and
(4) a female Tung Lieu Sz (陳利民), each of whom
was in possession of a bag of stolen flour, were
arrested whilst attempting to escape from the scene.
A further seven bags of flour were recovered
from the roadway where they had been dropped by

备注
（任何显著或特殊特征，由调查警官予以评注）。

1939年8月20日下午8时05分，本警署接到昌平路69号裕源新米面店的电话消息，称店外聚集了大量人群，且正在砸门。刑事侦缉处警探第242号、中央捕房警员第2734号及本人立即赶赴现场，发现约有500人的暴民冲击了该店，拆下了店铺正面及侧面的铁栅栏，强行撬开木制百叶窗，并正在从店内抢掠袋装面粉。
警方人员立即对暴民展开行动，并在刑事侦缉处警探第202号及其一名名为宋國忠 (Sung Koh Tsung) 的线民的协助下，成功驱散了暴民。（刑事侦缉处警探第202号当时休班，与其线民因看到人群而被吸引至现场。）
在驱散暴民主力后，已向警署通报情况，随后由格伦维尔 (Glanville) 巡官率领的另一队警力赶赴现场。
在驱散暴民的过程中，前四名被告，即(1) 尹長福 (Yung Zang Foh)、(2) 王秀英 (Wong Sau Yung)、(3) 慶長根 (Kyung Zang Kung) 以及 (4) 一名女性陳利民 (Tung Lieu Sz)，每人持有一袋被盗面粉，在试图逃离现场时被逮捕。
另有七袋面粉从道路上被追回，这些面粉系由

七名被告被带至巡捕房受讯时，均承认曾进入
投诉人处所并盗窃面粉，但均否认参与对店铺的实际
袭击，且均否认知晓从收银柜中盗窃30.00元一事。

经讯问，投诉人黄沃江（Wong Wo Kyang，音译）称，1939年8月20日晚7时30分左右，一群人开始在其店铺外聚集，店内存有265袋50磅装面粉及20袋120磅装大米。此数量的面粉和大米构成了投诉人的全部库存。

1939年8月20日晚8时，聚集的人群（约400人，其中大多数人显然来自附近地区，且多数为苦力阶层）开始表现出威胁性姿态。

1939年8月20日晚8时03分，在一群约十名手持棍棒的华籍苦力男子的带领下，人群袭击了该店铺。

在暴民袭击之前，投诉人已关闭所有百叶窗并锁上铁栅栏

一名台湾人因涉及日军当局在闸北扣留数袋大米引发的纠纷而被带至警局。

1940年12月16日下午3时15分，中央捕房警员编号1877将7名中国人和1名台湾人带至警局，事由是他们在爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）近四川路一带滋事，此事涉及13袋于1940年12月11日在闸北吴淞路桥被日本海军陆战队扣留的大米。

经刑事侦缉处警员编号185及具结人调查，查明事实如下：-

1940年12月11日，由17名中国人从乡下运往上海的13袋大米（价值700元），因未能取得许可证，在上述地点被日本当局扣留。

这17名中国米商的代表通过一名叫李德贵（Lee Teh Kwei）的中国人（已被带至警局）接触了一名名叫郑美苏（Ching Mei So）的台湾人。李德贵，46岁，天津人，职业为香烟店经理，住址为闸北吴淞路3号。他结识了这名台湾职员，并提出如果该台湾人能努力将被扣大米归还给中国业主，他们愿意支付300元作为酬谢。郑美苏，26岁，台湾人，职业为下级职员，受雇于上海市政府吴淞桥办事处，住址为四川北路附近金基里（Jin Chi Lee）南段206号。

先生：

1940年8月13日上午11时55分，巡捕2819号将一辆车牌号为 S.M.C. 23674 的卡车带至本警局。该车由张国英（Tsang Ke Zing）驾驶，其持有许可证第19724号，住址为罗宾森路812号。卡车上装载有53袋大米。

经刑事侦缉处3.176号警员及警佐103号 Baldeck 查询查明，1940年8月13日上午11时50分，上述巡捕在河南路近边界路执勤时，发现该卡车正准备离开租界进入苏州河以北地区（S.C.C.P.B.）管制区域，遂拦停卡车并要求司机出示运输大米的许可证。因司机未能按要求出示许可证，该巡捕便将载货卡车押送至本警局。

进一步查询显示，该批大米系日本米商加藤（Y.Kato）先生所有，其住址为四川北路806号。加藤是从位于爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）近河南路的中汇银行大楼内的益大（Yee Tah）公司购得此米。该批大米正从北苏州路1040号的中国仓库运往闸北宝山路13号。

根据克劳福德（Crawford）总监的指示，已允许该载货卡车（总检 1/8 1397）继续前往目的地。现呈报本报告以供知悉。

On 9.12.39. one coolie named Lieu Siau Pao (刘小保), who represented all the workers in the negotiation with the above mill management, is to be requested by the management through his guarantor named Lee Chi Ming (李志林) to resign. Sir,

At 10.20 a.m. on 13-9-39, C.P.Ce, 125 and 3172
brought to the station from North Soochow Road East of
Kiangse Road Bridge, 6 male Chinese for fighting the
particulars of whom are as follows:-

(1) Wong Fie Loong (黄兆龙), Shanghai, M/detective,
attached to Japanese Gendarmerie.

(2) Yih Yei Ming (葉一鳴), 23, Shanghai, M/detective,
as above.

(3) Daung Kuh Ming (唐光明), 26, Shanghai, M/detective
as above.

(4) Chen Lan Lee (陳蘭利), 55, Kompo, M/coolie, 7
Singapore Road.

(5) Hai Hyich Kwei (韓義奎), 21, Kompo, M/coolie,
7 Singapore Road.

(6) Loh Siah Kwei (羅雪貴), 56, Kompo, M/coolie,
Ferry Road.

Enquiries by C.D.C. 200 and U.S. Muir revealed
that the 3 first named are employed by Japanese
Gendarmerie to inspect the landing of cargoes of rice
to insure that a permit has previously been obtained
from the Japanese Authorities.

At about 8 a.m. they boarded a rice boat on the
Creek to enquire regarding the permit, however as the
owner of the rice was then not present they insisted
that the unloading of the rice, cease until the owner
appeared. This order was objected to by the last named
3 persons and many more coolies who were then engaged in
removing the rice, which eventually resulted in a quarrel

呈报人... U.S. Muir 转呈人... [签名] 主管警官，
负责人

先生：

1939 年 9 月 13 日上午 10 时 20 分，警员 C.P.Ce（编号 125 和 3172）将 6 名涉嫌斗殴的华籍男子从江西路桥以东的北苏州路带至本分局，其具体情况如下：

(1) Wong Fie Loong (黄兆龙)，上海人，男，侦探，隶属于日本宪兵队。

(2) Yih Yei Ming (葉一鳴)，23 岁，上海人，男，侦探，隶属同上。

(3) Daung Kuh Ming (唐光明)，26 岁，上海人，男，侦探，隶属同上。

(4) Chen Lan Lee (陳蘭利)，55 岁，高邮人，男，苦力，住新加坡路 7 号。

(5) Hai Hyich Kwei (韓義奎)，21 岁，高邮人，男，苦力，住新加坡路 7 号。

(6) Loh Siah Kwei (羅雪貴)，56 岁，高邮人，男，苦力，住斐伦路。

经刑事侦缉处警员 200 号及 U.S. Muir 调查查明，上述前三人受雇于日本宪兵队，负责检查大米货物的卸载情况，以确保事先已从日本当局获得许可证。

上午 8 时许，他们登上浜内的一艘米船查询许可证事宜，然而由于米主当时不在场，他们坚持要求停止卸米，直至米主出现。这一命令遭到最后列名的三人以及当时正在搬运大米的其他多名苦力的反对，最终导致了一场争吵

（批注：C? (完) 9 月 14 日. huxu/q 8D 9 月 14 日）

在驳船上爆发，最终在日本宪兵队介入后于北苏州路平息。
据苦力称，上述第一名人员在允许卸运大米之前索要20.00美元，此事发生在驳船上，但遭到便衣侦探否认。
在争吵过程中，便衣侦探受伤，并在雷士德华人医院接受治疗。所有医疗证明均注明为挫伤，伤势不重，未予拘留。
大米货主名为 Ung Sing Zung（音译），居住于新闸路，经查找已找到。该货主表示，卸米许可证目前由将大米运至上海的船东 Ah Yeh Tsoong（音译）持有。经查找后者，此情况得到证实，各方随后离开巡捕房，附属于日本宪兵队的便衣侦探认为此事已结。 A. Mui

Mr. Eveleigh, Manager of Messrs. Louis
Dreyfus & Co., was visited in connection with
the attached report and was asked to provide details
concerning the drivers and licence numbers of the
trucks alleged to have been detained by the Japanese
Naval Landing Party. Though promising to comply
with this request, Mr. Eveleigh has not, as yet, done
so and when reminded of his promise excused himself
by stating that he was experiencing difficulty in
obtaining the data required due to the fear of the
truck drivers that they might be involved in a dispute
with the Japanese Naval Landing Party. Mr. Eveleigh
does not explain his inability to provide the
Police with the licence numbers of the trucks.

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

Re alleged detention of several m/trucks with rice by the Japanese Naval Landing Party.

At 12 n on 9/12/39, instruction was received from D.O. "C" to make enquiries re several m/trucks loaded with saigon rice and which were detained by the J.N.L.P on the Garden Bridge.

Further information also was received from the Headquarters (Special Branch) that the rice is the property of the Dreyfus Company (French Firm) and same was transported from the Shanghai and Hongkew Wharf (S.S. "Doumer") to south of Creek.

It was also said that two m/trucks of rice were detained at about 3 p.m. 8/12/39, and two m/trucks some time in the morning on 9/12/39.

Immediately D.S. Ueoka and the undersigned visited the J.N.L.P. Headquarters and made enquiries.

Warrant officer Nakaseko who was in charge of all bridges (Garden, Chapoo and N. Szechuen) until 9 a.m. 9/12/39, was located and he said that no m/trucks loaded with rice were detained on 8/12/39.

The above officer also communicated with the officer who took charge of bridges from 9 a.m. 9/12/39 and later also said that no rice was detained on 9/12/39.

It was also learned that nothing could be detained or seized on any bridge without informing the officer i/c bridges.

S.C.G
(印：SHANGHAI COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE 18 JAN. 1940)
(批：See. Vide D. 8039 A/S(a)-7(7))

Early in November, 1939, the Mitsui Bussan
Kaisha and the Mitsubishi Shoji Kaisha were
authorized by the Japanese military authorities to
purchase 400,000 "zars" of rice at Sungkiang and
Wusieh respectively for consumption of Japanese
troops and also for the people of Japan and North
China. The rice dealers and hong owners in
those areas however showed their unwillingness to
sell to these people and the wholesale purchases
by the two Japanese firms were practically
unsuccessful. It is estimated that only 20,000
bags were purchased in the Wusieh area and 30,000
bags in the Sungkiang area and transported by rail
direct to Woosung, being exported from this point
to North China and Japan. The unwillingness on
the part of the dealers to sell to the Japanese was
brought about by the low prices offered for the
cereal and this attitude on December 1, 1939,
resulted in the suspension of export permits to
Chinese dealers transporting rice to Shanghai.
Consignments of rice (totalling some 25,000 bags)
which arrived in Shanghai on December 8, 9 and 10,
on the strength of export permits issued prior to
December 1, were detained at Markham Road Junction
and subsequently transported to Woosung by rail and
thence exported. Although the Japanese authorities

10th January 1940.

Monsieur M. Baudex,
Consul-General for France.
2, Rue du Consulat.
Shanghai.

Sir,

Re: SAIGON RICE TO SHANGHAI.

Please refer to our letter of the 31st December 1939, when we reported that in all, 3 lighters with about 1200 bags of Saigon Rice had been detained by some Japanese but were eventually released.

In the intervening 3 weeks we have had several further annoying incidents, but having successfully explained matters to the Japanese Naval and other Authorities, and believing that these explanations would free us from further annoyances, we did not report them to you. As we are again faced with a very serious situation as described below we are obliged to recount the following.

On Monday, the 8th instant, at about 1 P.M., 7 motor trucks, each loaded with about 40 to 45 bags Saigon Rice from the Shanghai & Hongkew Wharf. Co's Hunt's Wharf, Broadway, when trying to cross the Garden Bridge into the Central District, were arrested by the Japanese Gendarmerie and taken to their Headquarters on North Szechuan Road where the trucks with the rice, the drivers and the coolies were detained overnight and only released at about 11 A.M. on Tuesday, the 9th instant, and they came over to the Central District. The S.M.C. License numbers are:-

17398 - 23089 - 23465 - 16968 - 16534 - 16704 - 23096.

Our Mr. J. Lung spent a whole morning at the Gendarmerie Headquarters when he proved to the Officials that the rice was of French origin, imported by a French firm, and shipped by British steamer "Hannah Moller", and some by the Italian steamer "CORTELLAZZO" from Saigon to Shanghai, and it was only after very tedious waiting for a certain official to come to the office before the trucks were released. We believed then that this incident having been explained there would be no repetition and therefore did not wish to trouble you about the matter.

1940年1月10日。

M. Baudex 先生，
法国总领事。
领事馆路 2 号。
上海。

先生：

事由：西贡大米运往上海。

请参阅我方 1939 年 12 月 31 日的去函，当时我方报告称，共有 3 艘驳船载有约 1200 袋西贡大米，虽被某些日本人扣留，但最终获释。

在此后的三周内，我方又遭遇数起令人烦恼的事件，但鉴于已成功向日本海军及其他当局解释清楚，并相信这些解释能使我们要免受进一步的滋扰，故未向贵方报告。由于我方再次面临如下所述的严峻局势，现不得不陈述以下情况。

本月 8 日（星期一）下午 1 时许，7 辆卡车各装载约 40 至 45 袋来自上海与虹口码头公司百老汇路亨特码头（Hunt's Wharf）的西贡大米，在试图穿过外白渡桥进入中区时，被日本宪兵队拦截，并被带至北四川路的宪兵队总部。卡车、大米、司机及苦力均被扣留过夜，直至本月 9 日（星期二）上午 11 时许才获释，随后进入中区。上海工部局执照号码如下：

17398 - 23089 - 23465 - 16968 - 16534 - 16704 - 23096。

我方 J. Lung 先生在宪兵队总部耗费了整个上午，向官员们证明该批大米系法国产，由一家法国商行进口，并由英国轮船“Hannah Moller”号以及部分由意大利轮船“CORTELLAZZO”号从西贡运至上海。直到苦苦等待某位官员来到办公室后，卡车才得以放行。我方当时认为，既然此事已获解释，便不会重演，因此不愿为此事打扰贵方。

page_data.en:
To Monsieur M. Baudez,
Shanghai.
- 2 -
10/I/40.

Today a large number of trucks again went to the Shanghai & Hongker
Wharf Co's Hunt's Wharf, Broadway, to take delivery of further lots of
Saigon rice, and they were not interfered with until they reached the
Garden Bridge when they were not allowed to cross over the Bridge and
ordered to turn back. They were not arrested or detained as on the
8th instant, but as they were not allowed to cross the Bridge to the
Central District the trucks were obliged to return to the Wharf and
park there until a settlement is arrived at over this interference.

The Japanese Gendarmerie have explained that they cannot allow
transportation of any kind of rice over the Garden Bridge into the
Central District or into the French Concession without the trucks being
able to show some kind of a Pass issued by the Ta Tao Authorities
situated at the "Civic Centre at Kiangwan Road". This demand seems to
us very pretentious as we fail to see how any regulations which may be
issued by the Ta Tao Officials, outside of the area of the Foreign
Concessions, can be made applicable to foreign residents inside these
areas. We would ask your guidance as to whether we should apply for
such so-called "Passes."

The S.M.Police are evidently not able to help us in this matter,
and as a continuance of such interference of our freedom to trade in
foreign rice and to transport it within the area of the Foreign Concessions
is an infringement of our Treaty rights, we beg you, Sir, to make the
necessary representations as soon as possible at the correct quarters.

We beg to remain, Sir,

Yours obedient Servants,
P.P. LOUIS DREYFUS & Cie

AE/K.

c.c. Monsieur J. Brediam, Directeur Technique des Services Municipaux.
Mr. G. G. Phillips, Secretary, Shanghai Municipal Council.
Sir Robert Calder-Marshall, Chairman, S.M.C. Food Sub-Committee.
Mr. H. D. M. Robertson, Deputy Commissioner, S.M.P.

致 M. Baudez 先生，
上海。
- 2 -
1940年1月10日。

今日，又有大量卡车前往位于百老汇路的上海与虹口码头公司亨特码头（Hunt's Wharf），提运更多批次的西贡大米。这些卡车在抵达外白渡桥之前未受干扰，但在该处被禁止过桥，并被命令折返。它们并未像本月8日那样遭到逮捕或拘留，但由于不被允许过桥进入中区，卡车只得返回码头，并停泊在那里，直到就此次干扰事件达成解决方案为止。

日本宪兵队解释说，除非卡车能够出示由位于“江湾路市民中心”的大道政府当局签发的某种通行证，否则他们不允许任何种类的大米经外白渡桥运入中区或法租界。在我们看来，这一要求显得十分傲慢，因为我们看不出大道官员在外国租界区域之外颁布的任何规定，如何能适用于这些区域内的外籍居民。我们恳请阁下指导，我们是否应当申请这种所谓的“通行证”。

上海公共租界工部局警务处显然无法在此事上向我们提供协助，而且，持续干扰我们在外国租界区域内买卖和运输外国大米的自由，是对我们条约权利的侵犯。因此，我们恳请阁下尽快向有关方面提出必要的交涉。

此致，

您顺从的仆人，
代表 路易·德雷福斯公司（LOUIS DREYFUS & Cie）

AE/K.

 | RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.
 | Transportation of rice objected by Japanese Gendarme.
 | At 2.40 p.m. 10/1/40, F.P.S.11 on Garden Bridge duty reported at the station to the effect that between 2.15 pm and 2.20 pm even date, several m/trucks loaded with rice to be transported to a French firm, F.C. had been stopped and taken away by a Japanese Gendarme from the above bridge.
 | On receipt of the report, the undersigned proceeded to the Gendarmerie Headquarters, Bridge House, where the undersigned was told that the above stated cargo had not been detained there and they had not received any information regarding the affair.
 | At 4.20 pm 10/1/40, Mr. W.M.Mclennan, Deputy Supt. of the Shanghai & Hongkew Wharf Co. Ltd., accompanied by his Japanese interpreter Mr. M. Tanaka, came to the station and stated that the said m/trucks with the cargo had not been allowed by a Gendarme to pass over the bridge and the trucks driven back to the Hongkew Wharf where the rice had been ashored from a steamship arriving from Saigon.
 | Mr. Melennan requested assistance of a Japanese detective to proceed with them to the Japanese Gendarmerie Headquarters to give explanation regarding the ownership of the rice.

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

M/Trucks loaded with Saigon Rice detained by Japanese Gendarmes on Garden Bridge.

At 10.30 a.m. 9/1/40 the undersigned together with Mr. Jacques A Lang, an employee of the Louis Dreyfus & Co., proceeded to the Japanese Gendarmerie Headquarters, Bridge House, N. Szechuen Road where we interviewed Second Sub-lieutenant Ando who, in turn, told us that in case of Chinese owners, who wish to remove rice to the South of the Soochow Creek, they must first obtain permits from the Paymasters' Department of the Japanese Army.

The m/trucks loaded with Saigon rice have been detained by Japanese Gendarmes on Garden Bridge because none of the persons on the trucks could produce any permits or documents to prove the owners of the rice being foreigners.

As the owners of the rice have been found to be foreigners therefore the seven m/trucks loaded with rice were released at 11.50 a.m. this instant.

载有西贡大米之机动卡车在花园桥被日本宪兵扣留。

1940年1月9日上午10时30分，署名者会同路易斯·德雷福斯公司（Louis Dreyfus & Co.）雇员雅克·A·朗（Jacques A Lang）先生，前往北四川路大桥大楼的日本宪兵队总部，我们会见了安藤（Ando）二等少尉，他随即告知我们，若中国业主希望将大米运至苏州河以南，必须首先从日本陆军军需部门获得许可证。

载有西贡大米的机动卡车在花园桥被日本宪兵扣留，原因是卡车上的人员均无法出示任何许可证或文件以证明大米的所有者为外国人。

鉴于查明大米的所有者为外国人，因此七辆载有大米的机动卡车于当日上午11时50分获释。

| RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.
| M/trucks loaded with Saigon Rice detained by Japanese Gendarmes on Garden Bridge.
| At 3 p.m. 8/1/40, a telephone message was received from Louis Dreyfus & Co., 181 Kiangse Road stating that a great number of sacks containing Saigon rice loaded on several m/trucks had been taken away by Japanese Gendarmes from Garden Bridge and detained at their headquarters, Bridge House.
| Enquiries by the undersigned ascertained that the m/trucks had been detained on the ground that the Company failed to obtain permits from the Paymasters' Department of the Japanese Army at Civic Centre for the transportation of the above cargoes to south of the Soochow Creek.
| At 5 p.m. 8/1/40, the undersigned accompanied by one named Ching Shing Vung (金星文), an employee of the above Company, proceeded to the Bridge House and explained a provost sergeant Furuta that no permits had previously been required for any rice imported from abroad on presentation of "Bill of Lading".
| On the following explanation, the Gendarme, after obtaining the instructions from a senior officer, allowed one of the eight m/trucks to be released, however, the remaining seven m/trucks could not be permitted to go until their full investigations regarding the origin of the rice are completed.

S. I. REGISTRY
Stock of Rice in the Commercial Express 8039/A/5(0)-6
and Storage Company Godown, 480 Baikal Road D.
Date
December 18, 1939.

On December 12, 1939, 1,700 sacks of rice were
transported by motor truck to the godown of the
Commercial Express and Storage Company at 480 Baikal
Road and 300 large bales of cotton to the godown of
the same company at Chaoufoong Road, from lighters
tied alongside the Kwang Shing Public Jetty, Yangtzepoo
Road. On December 16, 1939, the 1,700 sacks of rice
were removed from 480 Baikal Road, and transported to
and stored in godowns owned by the Mitsui Bussan Kaisha
at Dixwell Road and East Broadway corner.

Another consignment of rice, consisting of 5,000
sacks, which arrived in Shanghai on December 14 and
were intended for unloading at the Kwang Shing Public
Jetty, Yangtzepoo Road, were later transported by river
to the M.B.K. godown at Dixwell Road and East Broadway
corner for storage.

According to information received by Yulin Road
Police Station from a person arrested on December 12,
1939 when a dispute arose over the transportation of
"the rice, the two consignments of rice mentioned in the
previous paragraph were brought to Shanghai from the
interior for delivery to Chinese owners residing south
of the Creek, but the M.B.K. company on learning of the
owners persuaded them to sell the entire lot to them
at their price. The first consignment of 1,700 sacks
being purchased at slightly over $32 per "zar." It
was also learned from this arrest that the instructions
for the seizure were issued by a Japanese subject
named N. Tsushima, Manager of the San Shin (三兴) Co.,
Exporters and Importers, Room No. 124A, Hardoon

贝加尔路480号D座商业快递与仓储公司仓库内的大米库存 8039/A/5(0)-6
日期
1939年12月18日。

1939年12月12日，1,700袋大米由卡车运至贝加尔路480号的商业快递与仓储公司（Commercial Express and Storage Company）仓库，另有300大包棉花运至该公司位于兆丰路（Chaoufoong Road）的仓库，上述货物均从停靠在杨树浦路广兴公码头的驳船上卸下。1939年12月16日，这1,700袋大米从贝加尔路480号移出，并运输至迪克斯韦尔路（Dixwell Road）与百老汇路（East Broadway）转角处由三井物产株式会社（Mitsui Bussan Kaisha）拥有的仓库存放。

另一批由5,000袋大米组成的货物于12月14日抵达上海，原计划在杨树浦路广兴公码头卸货，后经由水路运至迪克斯韦尔路与百老汇路转角处的三井物产株式会社仓库存放。

据玉林路警察局从一名于1939年12月12日因大米运输纠纷而被捕的人士处获得的情报显示，前文所述的两批大米系从内地运抵上海，拟交付给居住在苏州河以南的中国货主，但三井物产株式会社在得知货主身份后，说服他们以该公司定的价格将整批货物出售。第一批1,700袋大米的购买价格为每“zar”略高于32美元。从此名被捕者处还获悉，扣押指令是由一名日本籍人士N. Tsushima发出的，此人是三兴公司（San Shin Co.）的经理，该公司为进出口商，办公地点位于哈同路（Hardoon

Sir,

On the morning of December 10th 1938, the 1,700
sacks of rice were removed from the Commercial Express
and Storage Company Godown, 480, Baikal Road, and trans-
ported to and stored in godowns owned by the Mitsui
Bussan Kaisha, at Dixwell Road and East Broadway corner.

It was learned from Levin, that the M.B.K., had pre-
vailed upon the Chinese owners to sell the consignment
of rice to the company. Slightly over $62.00 per picul
was paid for the rice, which permitted the owners to
make only a very small percentage of profit.

It was further learned from Levin, that on December
14th 1939, N. Tsushima brought another consignment of
rice, consisting of 5,000 sacks, from the interior to
Shanghai. This consignment of rice was also intended
for delivery to the Chinese owners, in the South of the
Creek area, but once again the M.B.K. company stepped
in and purchased the entire lot.

This consignment of rice, which it had been intended
to unload at the Kwang Shing Public Jetty, Yangtsepoo
Road, is now being transported by river to the M.B.K.
godown at Dixwell Road and East Broadway corner, for

On November 15 and 16, 1939, some 625
bags of rice arrived at Markham Road Junction by
train from Wusih. Export of rice from this locality
is prohibited except by permission of the Japanese
authorities and it was subsequently ascertained that
this consignment had been dispatched by the Wusih
branch of the Yung Shing (永兴) Transport Co. of
761 South Soochow Road under a forged permit
purporting to have been issued to a Japanese named
Botoku Kichijima, c/o Kichiko Co., Wusih.

The Japanese Military Police then detained
375 bags still at the Junction and instituted
enquiries to trace the remaining 250 bags which
had already been delivered to the purchasers.

It was ascertained that 125 bags had been
delivered to the Yuen Mei (元美) Rice Hong at
344/13 Burkill Road, which on November 18 was visited
by a party of Japanese military police who nailed up
the room in which the rice was stored and informed
the occupants that the consignment would be removed
on the following day.

Taking with them two Chinese employees of
the Hong, the party proceeded to the Yah Chong Teh
Rice Hong
(协昌德) at 206 Avenue Road which concern had pur-
chased the remaining 125 bags. Of this number, 48
had been retailed in small quantities and 77 sold
to the Zung Foong Yoong (成丰永) Rice Hong at
754/102 Tsepoo Road by whom they had been stored in

Tsan Li (東服里) Scott Road and two employees of the
Nippon Transportation Co., North Szechuen Road.
According to Mr. Toyota, he had been away from
Shanghai in Wuhu on business from the 14-11-39 to the
17-11-39, when he returned to Shanghai on the evening
of the 17-11-39 he was questioned by the Japanese
Military Police as to whether he had recently transport-
ed rice from Wusieh to Shanghai. He had replied in the
negative because he knew that the Japanese Military had
a monopoly on all rice in Wusieh.
He was informed by the Military Police that a
cargo of 600 bags of rice had been despatched from
Wusieh to him in Shanghai on the 13-11-39 on 14-11-39.
The rice had been sent by railway to the Markham Road
Station and the Military Police had made enquiries and
found that 250 bags of the rice had already been
removed from that Station on the 15-11-39 while the
other 350 bags were still there. These 350 bags had

据丰田先生称，他因公务于 1939 年 11 月 14 日至 1939 年 11 月 17 日期间离开上海前往芜湖。当他于 1939 年 11 月 17 日晚回到上海时，日本宪兵队讯问他近期是否曾将大米从吴淞运至上海。他予以否认，因为他知道日本军方垄断了吴淞的所有大米。
宪兵队告知他，有一批 600 袋大米已于 1939 年 11 月 13 日至 14 日期间从吴淞发运给他本人（在上海）。该批大米经铁路运至马克姆路车站，经宪兵队查询发现，其中 250 袋已于 1939 年 11 月 15 日从该车站提走，其余 350 袋仍存于站内。这 350 袋大米已

been seized by the Military Police.
Mr. Toyota denied all knowledge of the rice and
it was then ascertained that the delivery permit
referring to the removal of the rice from Wusieh was
counterfeit. The delivery permit purported to show that
the rice had been sent to Shanghai by a Japanese named
Botoku Kichijima c/o Kichiko Co., Wusieh, who had
obtained the rice from the Yung Shih (永興) Rice Hong
in Wusieh, the manager of which hong is a Chinese named
Soong Sih Yang (宋錫揚), for delivery to Mr. Toyota
in Shanghai.
Mr. Toyota was suspected by the Military Police
of illegally bringing the rice to Shanghai because he
had previous dealings with the Yung Shing Rice Hong in
Wusieh. Therefore, Mr. Toyota and the Military Police
continued enquiries with a view to finding the 250 bags
of rice.
They succeeded in ascertaining through the Nyeu
Ping Kee (紐炳記) Transportation Co., 17 Canton Road,
who had transported the rice from the Markham Road
Station, that 125 bags of the rice had been taken to a
rice hong at Lane 344/13 Burkill Road and 125 bags to
a rice hong at 208 Avenue Road.
Mr. Toyota and Sergeant Take of the Military
Police went to these rice hongs on the afternoon of the
18-11-39. Enquiries at the first hong revealed that the
proprietor was absent.

大米由一名日本人名叫 Botoku Kichijima（音译），通过吴淞吉高公司（Kichiko Co.）寄往上海，此人已从吴淞永兴米行获得该批大米，该行经理为华人宋錫揚，目的是向上海的丰田先生交货。
宪兵队怀疑丰田先生非法将大米运入上海，因为他此前曾与吴淞永兴米行有过交易往来。因此，丰田先生与宪兵队继续进行调查，以期找到那 250 袋大米。
他们通过位于广东路 17 号的纽炳记运输公司成功查明，该公司曾从马克姆路站（Markham Road Station）运输该批大米，其中 125 袋被运至伯基尔路（Burkill Road）344/13 弄的一家米行，另外 125 袋被运至爱文义路（Avenue Road）208 号的一家米行。
1939 年 11 月 18 日下午，丰田先生与宪兵队的竹下警长（Sergeant Take）前往上述米行。在第一家米行的查询显示，店主不在。

At the second hong they questioned the

of the rice but he had re-sold 75 bags to the Zung Boong
Yoong (成丰永) Rice Hong at Lane 754/102 Tsaofoo Road;
the other 50 bags had been sold retail to customers.
They took the manager of this shop to the hong
on Tsaofoo Road and there interviewed the manager of that
hong who told them that the 75 bags of rice were then
stored in a godown at No. 777 North Honan Road. The manager
of this hong took them to the godown and showed them the
rice.
Mr. Toyota stated he explained to the rice
hong managers that the rice had been brought to Shanghai
by the illegal method and that the rice should
be handed over to the Military Police. He also told them
that he would send trucks to remove the rice from the
godown and the hong at 9.a.m. on the 19-11-39 and the
hong managers agreed to this, the manager of the hong on
Avenue Road also agreeing to make up the 50 bags which
he had already sold.
Regarding the other 125 bags of rice, these
are at present stored at the Yuan How (元茂) Rice Hong
at Lane 344/13 Burkill Road.
Two employees of this hong were arrested by
Mr. Toyota on the 18-11-39 and taken to the Military
Police in Hongkew because they were unable to give a
satisfactory statement regarding the rice.

在第二家米行，他们讯问了经理，查明该经理已收到125袋大米，但他已将其中75袋转售给位于曹福路（Tsaofoo Road）754弄102号的成丰永（Zung Boong Yoong）米行；其余50袋已零售给顾客。
他们将该店经理带至曹福路的米行，并在那里会见了该米行的经理，后者告知他们，这75袋大米目前存放在北河南路777号的一间仓库内。该米行经理随后带他们前往仓库，并向他们展示了大米。
丰田先生（Mr. Toyota）称，他向各米行经理解释，这批大米是通过非法途径运入上海的，应当移交给宪兵队。他还告诉他们，他将于1939年11月19日上午9时派卡车从仓库及米行运走大米，各米行经理对此表示同意，爱文义路（Avenue Road）米行的经理也同意补足其已售出的50袋大米。
至于另外125袋大米，目前存放在伯基尔路（Burkill Road）344弄13号的元茂（Yuan How）米行。
该米行的两名雇员因无法就大米来源作出令人满意的陈述，于1939年11月18日被丰田先生逮捕，并押送至虹口宪兵队。

1.

Illegal Functioning by Japanese.

At 5pm. on 18/11/39 the following persons came to
Sinza Station to report on the actions of three Japanese
and one Chinese:-
(1) Lee Tuh Fah(秦核孚), owner of the Yue Moh(元茂)
Rice Hong, No.13, Lane 344 Burkill Road.
(2) Tseu S Loh(徐世祿), employee of the Yah Tsang
Tuh(楊昌祥) Rice Shop, No. 208 Avenue Road.

On 15/11/39 each of the above received from the
Yoong Sing(永興轉運公司) Transportation Company, No. 761
Soochow Road, 125 bags of rice, the 1st informant
having this sent from Wusieh by the Tsang Yue Tau(張裕泰
) Rice Hong, and the 2nd informant from Wusieh by
the Yoong Sung(永生) Rice Hong.

Each has documents from the Hongs in Wusieh
asking them to accept delivery through the Transportation
Company. They have conducted business previously with
the above Hongs and always through the same Transportation
Company, which is Japanese controlled and which has an
Agency in Wusieh.

In regard to the above deliveries the two
informants have paid the purchase price to the
Transportation Company, $5000.00 in each case.

They admit that the Japanese Authorities have
placed a ban on the export of rice from Wusieh, but
did not believe this to be important as the

                           1939年11月18日

1.

日本人的非法活动。

1939年11月18日下午5时，下列人员来到新闸捕房，举报三名日本人及一名中国人的行为：
(1) 李笃发（秦核孚），伯基尔路344弄13号元茂米行业主。
(2) 徐世禄，爱文义路208号杨昌祥米店雇员。

1939年11月15日，上述二人各自从苏州路761号永兴转运公司收到125袋大米，其中第一举报人的大米由吴淞张裕泰米行经该公司运来，第二举报人的大米由吴淞永生米行经该公司运来。

二人均持有吴淞各米行出具的单据，要求他们通过该转运公司接收货物。他们此前曾与上述米行有过业务往来，且始终通过同一家转运公司进行交易，该公司由日本人控制，并在吴淞设有代理机构。

关于上述交货事宜，两名举报人均已向转运公司支付货款，每笔金额为5,000.00美元。

他们承认日本当局已禁止从吴淞出口大米，但认为此事并不重要，因为

Transportation Company was Japanese controlled.
At about 3pm. on 18/11/39 three Japanese and one
Chinese in civilian clothes entered the Hong of the
1st informant at No. 13, Lane 344 Burkill Road and
asked for the informant, who was absent. The accountant
admitted when questioned regarding the receipt of 125
bags of rice from Wusieh and was told by the Japanese,
through the Chinese as an interpreter, that the export
of rice from Wusieh was forbidden and that the rice
would have to be returned.
The callers then nailed up the front and rear door
of an inner room used to store the rice, and took the
following employees to a waiting motor car, licence
number unknown:
Dau Sing Di(陶心草), aged 30, native of Pootung,
accountant.
Ling Kwok Nyi(林国年), aged 21, native of Pootung,
shop-assistant.
The five remaining employees were warned not to
tamper with the rice and to tell their employer to be
present at 9am. on 19/11/39, when the 125 bags of rice
was to be removed.
The two employees were then driven off in the motor
car, which is described as of a yellow colour similar
to that used by Japanese Army Officials.
The 2nd informant reports that the three Japanese

该运输公司由日本人控制。
1939年11月18日下午3时许，三名日本人和一名身穿便服的中国人进入位于伯基尔路（Burkill Road）344弄13号的第一报案人商号，寻找该报案人，但其当时不在。会计在接受关于从吴淞接收125袋大米的询问时予以承认，随后日本人通过那名中国人作为翻译告知他，禁止从吴淞出口大米，这些大米必须退回。
来访者随即将一间用于存放大米的内室的前后门钉死，并将下列雇员带至一辆等候的汽车上，车牌号码不详：
陶心草（Dau Sing Di），30岁，浦东人，会计。
林国年（Ling Kwok Nyi），21岁，浦东人，店员。
其余五名雇员受到警告，不得擅动大米，并被告知通知其雇主于1939年11月19日上午9时到场，届时将运走这125袋大米。
这两名雇员随后被汽车载离，据描述该车为黄色，与日本军方官员使用的车辆颜色相似。
第二报案人报告称，那三名日本人

and one Chinese arrived outside his shop in the motor

以及一名华人于1939年11月18日下午约3时30分乘汽车抵达其店铺外。
有人问他是否从Musleh（音译）处购买了125袋大米，他承认确有其事，并称已将其中77袋大米转售给乍浦路754弄102号一家米行的店主。
随后，他被要求进入汽车，他也照做了，并注意到车上有第一名线人的两名雇员。
一行人随即前往乍浦路754弄102号的米行，该米行店主告知日本人，他将大米存放在苏州路777号的一座仓库内。随后，该店主也进入汽车，陪同一行人前往仓库，对大米进行了检查。
他和第二名线人随后被释放，并被告知须于1939年11月19日上午9时到达仓库，届时将运走大米。第二名线人还被告知，他必须交出剩余的48袋大米。
汽车随后向虹口方向驶去，第一名投诉人的雇员随同前往。
相关情况已通报给“B”区巡官，根据其指示，将于1939年11月19日在伯基尔路344弄13号及爱文义路208号部署警卫。

关于从吴淞非法运输大米一案，兹报告如下：负责此案的宪兵队已返回吴淞，本人承蒙当地宪兵司令部的好意协助，通过军用长途电话与其取得联系。据其告知，因其无权与上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）进行交涉，故将请示其上级军官，就移交涉案大米一事提出正式请求。

Mr. Toyoda expressed his regret that the Transport-

其雇主被指控非法运输大米，因而被召至日本宪兵队总部。提货单盖有苏州南路761号永盛公司（Yung Shing and Co.）的印章，系从林先生（Mr. Hayashi）处借得，现附于本函之后。

当被问及为何尽管提货单上明确注明收货人为K. Toyoda，货物却交付给一家华商企业永盛公司时，林先生称，他并未怀疑其中有任何不当行为，因为出示该文件的人与他十分熟识，且是K. Toyoda先生的雇员。

Toyoda先生对运输公司凭未经其正式签署的提货单交付货物表示遗憾。林先生对此予以反驳，理由是Toyoda先生此前并未报备需使用特定的印章或签名。

据悉，军方当局将不对K. Toyoda采取任何行动，因为经其调查查明，他与此案无关。

November 20, 1939.

Mr. Uyehara,
Deputy Commissioner,
S. M. P.

Sir,

Petition Re illegal transportation of rice stock
within the control system enforced by the Imperial
Japanese Army, by falsely representing the petitioner.

Name: Kyuma Toyota, age 42.
Permanent Domicile: No. 30, Kenya-cho, Kanda-Ku, Tokyo.
Present Address: No. 51 Tung Chao Lee, Scott Road, Shanghai.

By falsely representing the petitioner as the consignee,
600 bags of rice were transported from Wusieh (蕪) to
Shanghai, and 250 bags out of this number were received by
the "Yung Shing" and Company (永興公司) through the business
office of the Nippon Tsuun Kaisha by means of a falsified
receipt. The "Yung Shing" and Company transported the cargo
into the International Settlement.

Accordingly, the petitioner, as the consignee named in
the receipt, has been interrogated by the Japanese Gendarmerie
in Wusieh (      ) on a charge of illegal transportation of
rice by means of a false "Transportation Certificate".

The petitioner wishes to emphasize that he is not at all
implicated in this affair. He is well aware that at present
he can not buy rice in the districts under the control of the
Japanese Army without first obtaining a valid "Purchasing
Certificate" issued by the Japanese Military Special Service
Mission as well as one issued by the Asia Development Board.

On the early morning of November 14, the petitioner
started for Wuhu (湖) by an express train and on the
following day proceeded to the Wuhu sub-office of the
Japanese Consulate-General, with a view to applying for a
trading permit for my branch shop in that city.
page_data.zh:
1939年11月20日。

上原先生，
副总监，
上海公共租界工部局警务处。

敬启者：

关于在帝国日本军队实施的管制体系内，通过虚假陈述申诉人身份而非法运输大米库存的请愿书。

姓名：Kyuma Toyota（音译），年龄42岁。
永久住址：东京神田区绀屋町30号。
现住址：上海斯科特路同兆里51号。

通过将申诉人虚假陈述为收货人，600袋大米从芜湖运至上海，其中250袋由“永兴公司”通过日本通运株式会社的营业所，凭伪造的收据接收。“永兴公司”将该批货物运入公共租界。

因此，申诉人作为收据上列明的收货人，因涉嫌使用伪造的“运输证”非法运输大米，已在芜湖接受日本宪兵队的讯问。

申诉人希望强调，他与此事毫无牵连。他深知，目前在日军控制区内购买大米，必须首先获得日本军方特务机关签发的有效“购买证”，以及兴亚院签发的相应证件。

11月14日凌晨，申诉人乘快车前往芜湖，并于次日前往日本总领事馆芜湖分馆，旨在为其在该市的分店申请贸易许可证。

page_data.en:
- 2 -

Two days hence, i.e. on November 16, the petitioner
proceeded to the wharf sub-office of the Japanese Gendarmerie
in Wuhu and made the report to the effect that he had already
applied to the Consular Authorities for permission to open a
branch office in Wuhu.

On the morning of November 17, the petitioner left the
town by train, returning home at about 8.50 p.m. the same
day. Upon arrival here he was told that a member of the
Settlement Detachment of the Japanese Gendarmerie had called
both at his house and also his shop in Paoshan Road ( 宝山路 ),
Chapei, and ordered his immediate attendance at the Gendarmerie
Headquarters as soon as he returns home.

At 8.30 a.m. on November 18, just as he had telephoned to
the Settlement Detachment of the Japanese Gendarmerie, a
telephone call was received from the business office of the
Nippon Tsuun Kaisha located at the Markham Road Railway Yard
requesting him to go to the office, as gendarmes were waiting
for his presence there in connection with a case involving
transportation of rice.

Being ignorant of what had happened during his absence
from this city, the petitioner hurried to the office only to
be told that the Gendarmerie Authorities were now making
arrangements to interrogate him.

Searching enquiries instituted by the authorities elicited
the fact that the petitioner had been accused as the consignee
responsible for the illegal transportation of a cargo of rice.

It was a great shock to the petitioner and being highly
incensed over this false accusation, he made every possible
endeavour to defended his case. The fact remains, however,
that the rice in question had already been carelessly given
out to an unauthorized consignee by the Nippon Tsuun Kaisha.

There, in order to establish his innocence, the petitioner
resolved to ascertain the whereabouts of the cargo of rice so
that the 250 bags reported as having been misappropriated
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

两天后，即11月16日，申诉人前往芜湖日本宪兵队码头分遣队办事处，提出报告，称其已向领事当局申请在芜湖开设分处的许可。

11月17日上午，申诉人乘火车离开该镇，于同日晚上约8时50分返家。抵达此处后，他被告知，日本宪兵队租界分遣队的一名成员曾先后到访其住宅及其位于闸北宝山路（ Paoshan Road ）的店铺，并命令其回家后立即前往宪兵队总部报到。

11月18日上午8时30分，正当他致电日本宪兵队租界分遣队时，他接到位于马霍路（ Markham Road ）铁路货场的日本通运株式会社（ Nippon Tsuun Kaisha ）营业所打来的电话，要求他前往该处，因为宪兵正就一起涉及大米运输的案件在那里等候他。

由于不知晓其离沪期间发生之事，申诉人匆忙赶至营业所，却仅被告知宪兵当局正在安排对其进行讯问。

经当局深入调查，查明申诉人被指控为负责非法运输一批大米的收货人。

这对申诉人来说是一个巨大的打击，他对这一诬告感到极为愤怒，并竭尽全力为自己辩护。然而，事实是，涉案大米已被日本通运株式会社疏忽地交付给了一名未经授权的收货人。

因此，为了证明自己的清白，申诉人决定查清该批大米的下落，以便找回据报被挪用的250袋大米

page_data.en:
- 3 -
may be recovered and returned to the Gendarmerie Authorities.
Realizing the possibility of dangers and other complic-
ations in the Settlement, the petitioner accompanied a
gendarme from Wusieh and proceeded to make enquiries at the
"Yung Shing" and Company, the alleged consignee, where we
were told that the said company meanwhile had removed to the
Hsing Hwa Hotel ( 新華旅館 ). The hotel was next visited
and observations were maintained in order to locate the
whereabouts of Soong Ching Yang ( 宋錦楊 ).
We were informed that the Chinese had already left the
hotel. As the petitioner emerged from the hotel and walked
into the street, by chance he ran into a man who had been
formerly employed by the "Yung Shing" and Company. He was
asked whether he could throw any light as to the present
whereabouts of Soong Ching Yang in question and gave the
information that the party had left for Wusieh on November 16.
By interrogating this man who had taken part in the
transportation of rice, we became aware of the fact that one
Heu Ping Kee ( 金炳記 ), who is in transportation business
and residing at House No. A 6, Lane No. 126, Szeohmen Road,
was responsible for the removal of the cargo in question.
The petitioner then went back immediately to the
Markham Road Railway Yard and succeeded in locating a Chinese
named Woo ( 吳 ) a go-between in this illegal transaction.
This man subsequently led the petitioner to various places
where the rice had been taken and all the bags were eventually
located and identified.
The first address visited was Yuen Mow Hong ( 元茂號 )
Burkill Road, where 125 bags of Wusieh rice were found.
However, the employees of the hong at first closed the
front door in spite of the petitioner's request to be admitted
to the premises, so the petitioner and his companion went round
to the back door of the hong and quietly asked for an interview
with the master on the pretext that he was a forwarding agent,
introducing a rice merchant for a bonafide business transa-
page_data.zh:
- 3 -
以便追回并归还给宪兵当局。
鉴于租界内可能存在危险及其他复杂情况，申请人随同一名来自吴淞的宪兵，前往据称的收货人“永盛公司”（Yung Shing and Company）进行查询。在那里我们得知，该公司已迁至新华旅馆（Hsing Hwa Hotel）。随后我们前往该旅馆，并进行监视，以确定宋锦杨（Soong Ching Yang）的下落。
我们获悉，该名华人已离开旅馆。当申请人走出旅馆来到街上时，偶然遇到一名曾受雇于“永盛公司”的男子。经询问其是否能提供有关宋锦杨目前下落的线索，该男子告知，此人已于11月16日前往吴淞。
通过讯问这名参与大米运输的男子，我们得知，从事运输业务、居住在西门路126弄A6号的许炳记（Heu Ping Kee，音译：金炳記），负责搬运涉案货物。
随后，申请人立即返回马克姆路（Markham Road）铁路货场，成功找到一名姓吴（Woo）的华人，此人是该非法交易的中间人。此人随后带领申请人前往大米被运往的各个地点，最终所有米袋均被找到并确认。
首先探访的地址是伯基尔路（Burkill Road）的元茂号（Yuen Mow Hong），在那里发现了125袋吴淞大米。然而，尽管申请人要求进入 premises，该商号的员工起初仍关闭了前门，因此申请人及其同伴绕至商号后门，假称自己是货运代理人，为一位米商介绍一笔正当的商业交易，以此为由quietly请求与店主面谈。

page_data.en:
- 4 -

ction. The idea was to ascertain the quantity of rice in
stock there and also its origin.

The reply was very vague and extremely evasive. They
told us the master of the Hong was away making purchases
elsewhere.
forthcoming
As no definite answer was/from the shop-assistants, the
petitioner indicated to them his intention of demanding the
handing over of the cargo of rice on the grounds that it had
been removed without authority. However, on the plea of the
shopkeeper's absence, the assistants refused to comply with
this demand.

In consequence thereof, the petitioner was obliged to
nail down the room where the rice had been stored and to take
charge of the key for the front door pending the settlement
of the matter for it was his idea to exonerate himself from
this infamous charge levelled against him. The petitioner
warned the men that no one will be allowed to remove the cargo.

As the petitioner became aware of the proprietor's hasty
flight, at about 5.30 p.m. the same day, he accompanied two of
the employees to the Japanese Gendarmerie, with a view to
proving his innocence in the case. He resorted to this step
realizing that it would be best for the Gendarmerie Authorities to
enquire for themselves.

Here the assistants were warned by the petitioner who
advised them to speak the truth, for they would then be released
as soon as the case is cleared up.

Although the petitioner felt very sorry for the two
Chinese, yet he was obliged to take the steps as outlined above
in order to exonerate himself from the blame.

The management of the Yah Chong Tah Rice Shop (悠昌德米店),
the next receiver of the illegally obtained rice, where 125
bags of the rice were reportedly transported from the Yung Shing
and Company, asserted that no rice was left in stock and that
50 bags of rice have already been disposed of in retail
page_data.zh:
- 4 -

行动。其目的是查明该处库存大米的数量及其来源。

回复非常含糊且极力回避。他们告诉我们，该商号的经理外出到别处采购去了。
即将
由于店员未能给出明确答复，申请人向他们表明，他打算要求移交这批大米，理由是该批货物系未经授权而被移走。然而，店员以店主不在为由，拒绝配合这一要求。

因此，申请人不得不将存放大米的房间钉死，并在事件解决之前掌管前门的钥匙，因为他意在洗清加诸于他的这项恶名昭著的指控。申请人警告那些人，任何人不得移走该批货物。

由于申请人意识到店主已匆忙潜逃，同日约下午5时30分，他陪同两名雇员前往日本宪兵队，以期证明自己在该案中的清白。他采取这一步骤，是认识到最好由宪兵当局自行进行调查。

在此，申请人警告了店员，劝告他们讲真话，因为一旦案情查清，他们便会立即获释。

尽管申请人对这两名中国人深感同情，但他仍不得不采取上述步骤，以洗清自己的罪责。

悠昌德米店（Yah Chong Tah Rice Shop）的管理层——据称从永盛公司（Yung Shing and Company）运来125袋非法所得大米的下一接收方——声称库存中已无大米，且已有50袋大米通过零售方式处置完毕

page_data.en:
- 5 -

business.

The petitioner explained to the men in the rice shop regarding the particulars of the illegally acquired rice and demanded an explanation and asked them to produce evidence as to how the cargo came to be in their possession and how it was disposed of.

Eventually, it was disclosed by the inmates that the rest of the stock numbering 75 bags, had been sold to the Zung Foong Yung Hong (成豐永號), NO. 102, Tsapoo Road.

Thereupon, taking with him a representative of the Yah Sheng Tah Rice Shop, the petitioner went to the Zung Foong Yung Hong, where he was informed that the cargo in question was placed in storage at the No. 2 Godown of the Bank of Shanghai, No. 777, Soochow Road. The godown was next visited and the information verified.

Having succeeded in locating the entire cargo of the illegally transported bags of rice, the petitioner immediately got in touch with the Nippon Tsuun Kaisha over the telephone requesting them to send a motor truck, but owing to the interruption of telephone service, this was unsuccessful.

The Zung Foong Yung Hong management were warned regarding purchasing of illegally acquired rice with the full knowledge of the circumstances of the theft and persuaded to hand over the cargo to the petitioner the following morning as the circumstances would be against them should they refuse to comply with this request.

Hitch in Recovery of Cargo.

At 9 a.m. on November 19, the petitioner in company with gendarmes despatched from the Japanese Gendarmerie Detachment in Wusieh, went to the No. 2 Godown of the Bank of Shanghai, taking with him 20 coolies in five motor trucks owned by the Nippon Tsuun Kaisha and proceeded to make arrangements for the taking over of the cargo in question. Presently, Mr. R. Robertson, D.O. "A" and several other officers of the S.M.P.
page_data.zh:
- 5 -

业务。

申诉人向米店内的伙计说明了非法获取大米的具体情况，要求他们作出解释，并出示证据说明这批货物是如何落入他们手中以及如何处置的。

最终，店内人员透露，其余库存共计75袋，已出售给位于乍浦路102号的成豐永號（Zung Foong Yung Hong）。

随后，申诉人带着亚生大（Yah Sheng Tah）米店的一名代表前往成豐永號，在那里他被告知，涉案货物存放在苏州路777号上海银行第二仓库。随后他们前往该仓库，核实了这一信息。

在成功 locating 全部非法运输的大米后，申诉人立即通过电话与日本通运会社（Nippon Tsuun Kaisha）联系，请求派遣一辆卡车，但由于电话服务中断，未能成功。

成豐永號的管理层因在完全知晓盗窃情节的情况下购买非法所得大米而受到警告，并被说服于次日上午将货物移交给申诉人，因为如果他们拒绝配合这一要求，局势将对他们不利。

货物追回过程中的波折。

11月19日上午9时，申诉人与从吴淞日本宪兵分队派出的宪兵一同，乘坐日本通运会社拥有的五辆卡车，带着20名苦力，前往上海银行第二仓库，着手安排接管涉案货物。不久，公共租界工部局警务处“A”区副督察 R. Robertson 先生及其他几名警官到达。

page_data.en:
- 6 -
arrived at the scene.
Addressing the officer with due respect, the petitioner
acquainted Mr. H. Robertson with the particulars of the case
and the officer declared that he could not allow any one, no
matter what his nationality might be, to remove the rice in
question.
pending enquiries
On the guarantee that the cargo would be left intact, the
party left the godown.
In view of the foregoing, the steps taken by the petitioner
might be subject to criticism, but he is convinced that under the
circumstances he had no alternative but to have recourse to such
a measure in order to establish his innocence.
It is true that the petitioner might as well have approached
the Japanese Branch of the S.M.P. for assistance in the first
place, but he was obliged to omit this procedure.
The petitioner, should, therefore, be much obliged if you
would kindly appreciate the steps taken by him, for whatever he
did, he meant to be well and it was far from his intention to
offend any one.

Yours faithfully,

Sealed: K. Toyota.
page_data.zh:
- 6 -
抵达现场。
申请人以应有的恭敬态度向警官陈述，并向 H. Robertson 先生告知了本案的详细情况，该警官声明，无论国籍为何，均不允许任何人移走涉案大米。
待调查期间
在保证货物保持原状的前提下，相关人员离开了仓库。
鉴于上述情况，申请人所采取的步骤或许会受到非议，但他深信，在此情形下，他别无选择，只能诉诸此类措施以证明自身清白。
诚然，申请人本可首先向工部局警务处日本分部寻求协助，但他不得不省略此程序。
因此，若蒙阁下体谅申请人所采取的步骤，申请人将不胜感激；其所作所为皆出于善意，绝无意冒犯任何人。

此致，

盖章：K. Toyota（音译）。

日期：1939年11月28日 4 / 11 39
事由：日本宪兵及日本平民企图从苏州路777号仓库夺取大米。
呈报人：副督察长 Elders。转呈人：巡官 Du Cheng Lo。11/2。

先生，

遵照“A”分区副总监的指示，
副督察长 Elders 和刑事侦缉股警员336号就本案涉及老闸区的华人方面情况进行了进一步调查。调查结果如下：-

位于苏州路777号的仓库归上海商业储蓄银行有限公司所有。爱文义路208号的杨昌德（Yah Tsang Tuh）米店租用该仓库存放大米。他们这样做已有一年多。

该米店一名名为张心才（Tsang Sing Zai）的雇员驻守仓库，负责看管大米，并记录大米的进出情况。大米的进出不由仓库业主检查，仅由上述米店雇员检查。

已从该男子处取得一份陈述（附副本），从中可知，125袋大米于1939年11月15日下午3点左右运抵仓库。这些大米由吴淞永兴（Yoong Sing）运输公司发送。将大米运至仓库的人持有一张送货单，负责仓库的张心才（Tsang Sing Zai）由此得知这125袋大米来自吴淞的永生（Yoong Sung）米行。他在该送货单上签字，随后送货单被运米人员带走。随后他在账簿中登记了这125袋大米

I am the owner of the Zung Foong Yoeng (成丰永) Rice
Shop located at Lane 754/102 Tiendong Road. I daily visit
the rice market at the Ching Liu Koh (青蓮閣) Teashop 515
Foochow Road, in order to make transactions.

At 10 a.m. 16-11-39 I visited the market as usual
when one named Tsang Ts Nyi (張子宜) broker of the Yah
Tsong Tuh (場昌德) Rice Shop, 209 Avenue Road, approached,
stating that he had 75 sacks of rice for sale, each weighing
160 catties, total value $3,348.10, at the same time he showed
me the sample of rice. I agreed to purchase these but I
have not yet paid the money. He then issued a receipt
and handed it over to me, it was a receipt by which the
goods could be obtained.

At 10 a.m. 18-11-39 one named Tseh S Loh (祝世祿),
employee of the Yah Tsong Tuh Rice Shop, informed me by
telephone to the effect that the above mentioned 75 sacks
of rice had been deposited in an upstairs room at Shanghai
Godown No.2 located at 777 Soodlow Road and I was allowed
to take away the goods at any time.

by two Japanese came to my shop and asked me whether I had
taken away the above mentioned 75 sacks of rice from the
said Godown. To this I made a negative reply. The two
Japanese then told me they intended to go to the said
Godown at 9 a.m. the following day (19-11-39).

以下为本人于1939年11月21日在老闸捕房录取、由书记员顾廷怡（Koo Ting I，音译）翻译的浙江籍已婚人士王成（Wong Hwai Zung），29岁的供词。

我是位于天潼路754弄102号“成丰永”米行的业主。我每日前往福州路515号青莲阁茶楼的米市进行交易。

1939年11月16日上午10时，我照常前往米市，当时有一名自称张子宜（Tsang Ts Nyi，音译）的人前来接洽，他是爱文义路209号“场昌德”（Yah Tsong Tuh，音译）米行的经纪人。他声称有75包大米出售，每包重160斤，总价为3,348.10元，同时向我展示了米样。我同意购买，但尚未付款。随后他开具了一张提货单并交给我，凭此单可提取货物。

1939年11月18日上午10时，“场昌德”米行雇员祝世禄（Tseh S Loh，音译）通过电话通知我，称上述75包大米已存于苏州路777号上海第二仓库（Shanghai Godown No.2）的楼上房间内，我可随时前往提货。

1939年11月18日下午3时30分，祝世禄（Tseh S Loh，音译）陪同两名日本人来到我的店中，询问我是否已从上述仓库提走那75包大米。我予以否认。那两名日本人随即告诉我，他们打算于次日（1939年11月19日）上午9时前往该仓库。

以上供词属实。

Date 21 / 11 / 39

CHINA PRESS.

NOV 21 1939

U.S. Marines Guard Rice
Hongs Visited By Japanese

Guards of the Fourth U.S. Marines yesterday reinforced members of the Shanghai Municipal Police patrolling outside two rice hongs in the Sinza district which last Saturday were visited by Japanese, allegedly in search of smuggled rice.

Altogether three rice hongs were visited Saturday by three Japanese, the third being located in the Louza district. In all cases the Japanese, said to consist of a gendarme from Wusih and two Japanese employees of a transportation firm, nailed up the back doors and locked the main entrances of the hongs.

The hongs in question are situated at 13, lane 344 Burkill Road, 208 Avenue Road and 377 West Soochow Road. The latter hong was again visited by the Japanese Sunday morning, when an S.M.P. Chinese constable, who questioned the trio, was on guard.

Informed of the visits, the S.M.P. posted guards, while Marines sent out light detachments to reinforce the S.M.P. constables at the entrances of the two hongs within their defense sector.

It was believed yesterday that the Japanese were attempting to track down rice which had been brought to Shanghai on forged passes. Further reports stated that Japanese authorities are attempting to monopolize rice from the lower Yangtse Basin for transportation to Japan and Korea in view of the shortage there.

Meanwhile, it was revealed by an S.M.C. official yesterday that the present stock of rice in Shanghai was estimated at approximately 224,000 piculs, a total considerably higher than the 50,000 piculs here last September, when prices rose to more than $50 per picul.

Because of the recent improvement in the exchange, it was stated, a number of orders have been placed with Indo-China. One firm is said to have ordered 500 tons of Saigon rice.

Liu
Koh

《字林西报》。

1939年11月21日

美国海军陆战队守卫米行
日本人探访米行

昨日，第四团美国海军陆战队的卫兵增援了在上海公共租界警务处巡逻人员，后者在辛家花园（Sinza）区两家米行外执行巡逻任务；上周六，日本人曾到访这两家米行，据称是为了搜查走私大米。

周六共有三家米行被三名日本人探访，第三家位于老闸（Louza）区。在所有这些案例中，据说日本人由一名来自无锡的宪兵和一家运输公司的两名日本雇员组成，他们将米行的后门钉死，并锁上了正门。

涉事米行分别位于伯基尔路（Burkill Road）344弄13号、爱文义路（Avenue Road）208号以及苏州河西路377号。周日早晨，日本人再次探访了最后提到的这家米行，当时一名负责盘问这三人的华捕正在那里站岗。

获悉这些探访情况后，上海公共租界警务处部署了警卫，同时海军陆战队派出小型分队，增援其防区内两家米行入口处的上海公共租界警务处巡捕。

昨日人们认为，日本人正试图追踪那些持伪造通行证运抵上海的大米。另有报告称，鉴于日本和朝鲜的大米短缺，日本当局正试图垄断长江下游地区的大米，以便运往日本和朝鲜。

与此同时，一位工部局官员昨日透露，估计上海目前的大米库存约为224,000担，这一总数远高于去年9月的50,000担，当时米价涨至每担50美元以上。

据悉，由于近期汇率改善，已向印度支那下达了一些订单。据说有一家公司订购了500吨西贡大米。

刘
柯

Date 21 / 11 / 39

Hwa Pao, Ta Mei Pao, Sin Wan Pao, Shun Pao, and Ta Mei Wan Pao :-

21.11.39 (AM) JAPANESE ENDEAVOUR TO PREVENT SETTLEMENT RICE SHOPS FROM OPERATING

Recently a consignment of 125 bags of rice was secured by the Ya Chong Tuh Rice Shop (協昌德米號) at No. 206 Avenue Road from merchants' in Wulsh. It was transported here by the Yung Shing Transportation Company (永興轉運碼). Unexpectedly on the day following the arrival of this consignment, three officials of the Japanese authorities called at the shop and demanded an inspection of the transportation permit for this consignment.
Alleging that the permit was a counterfeit, the officials declared that the shop was not allowed to sell the rice and attempted to remove the whole consignment.

On the ground that the question of transportation permit is one that concerns the transportation company but has nothing to do with the shop responsible for the disposal of the rice, the shop assistants refused to comply with the demand of the Japanese. Subsequently, the Police were notified whereupon three Chinese constables were detailed to the shop for purposes of protection. As the shop is situated in the American Defence Sector, American marines were likewise despatched to the place for protection purposes in co-operation with the Police.

The shop has also 75 bags of rice stored in the godown of the Shanghai Commercial & Savings Bank. The shop has been notified by the Police not to withdraw this stock prior to the solution of the trouble and has been told to ring up the Police any time when disputes take place over this matter.

A similar incident recently took place at the Yuan Mou Rice Shop (元茂米号), No. 13, Lane 344, Burkill Road, and protection has therefore likewise been given to it by the American marines and the Police.

《华报》、《大美报》、《新晚报》、《申报》及《大美晚报》：

1939年11月21日（上午）日本人企图阻止租界内米店营业

近日，位于爱文义路（Avenue Road）206号的協昌德米號从吴淞的商人处购得一批大米，共计125袋。该批大米由永興轉運碼负责运输至本店。不料，在该批货物抵达后的次日，三名日本当局官员来到店内，要求检查该批货物的运输许可证。
日方官员声称该许可证系伪造，宣称该店不得出售此批大米，并试图将整批货物搬走。

店员以运输许可证问题关乎运输公司，而与负责销售大米的店铺无关为由，拒绝服从日本人的要求。随后，警方接到通知，随即派遣三名华捕前往该店执行保护任务。由于该店位于美军防区，美国海军陆战队亦派员前往该地，与警方协同执行保护任务。

该店另有75袋大米存放于上海商业储蓄银行的仓库中。警方已通知该店，在纠纷解决之前不得提取此库存，并告知若因此事发生争执，可随时致电警方。

近日，伯基尔路（Burkill Road）344弄13号的元茂米号也发生了类似事件，因此美国海军陆战队与警方同样向其提供了保护。

CENTRAL POLICE Station.
July. 3 192 1

REPORT ON Stocks of rice in rice shops in Shanghai

Made by D. S. I. Kay Forwarded by Director of Crime Intelligence.

Sir,

In the Central district there are four rice shops. Three of these have no stock in hand whilst the other shop has six hundred piculs, three hundred of which are in a godown at 529 Tiendong Road.

In the Louza district there are 38 rice shops, none of which have any rice in stock.

There are fifty eight rice shops in the Hongkow district. Fifty five of these have no rice at all in stock. Three have thirty three and a half piculs in all, distributed in quantities of three and a half to twenty piculs.

Sinza district contains forty five rice shops and one rice hong, all of which are without stocks.

There are 17 rice shops in the Bubbling Well district. Five of these have no rice at all in stock. The others have forty nine and a half piculs in quantities of one to ten piculs.

In the Gordon Road district there is a total quantity of sixty eight piculs distributed over seventeen rice shops, in quantities ranging from one to fourteen piculs. Nine shops in this district have no rice in stock.

There are forty rice shops and one rice hong in the West Hongkow district. Thirteen of the former have no stock in hand, whilst the others have quantities ranging from one to thirty four piculs, amounting in the aggregate to two hundred and forty one piculs. The one rice hong contains fifty piculs.

关于上海米店大米库存的报告

由警司 D. S. I. Kay 制作，经犯罪情报处处长转呈。

敬启者：

在中央区共有四家米店。其中三家无现货库存，另一家存有六百担，其中三百担存放于天潼路529号的仓库内。

在老闸区共有三十八家米店，均无大米库存。

在虹口区共有五十八家米店。其中五十五家完全无库存。另外三家共有三十三担半，数量从三担半至二十担不等。

新闸区共有四十五家米店和一家米行，均无库存。

在静安寺区（Bubbling Well district）共有十七家米店。其中五家完全无大米库存。其余各家共存有四十九担半，每家数量从一担至十担不等。

在戈登路区（Gordon Road district），十七家米店共存有六十八担大米，每家数量从一担至十四担不等。该区有九家米店无库存。

在西虹口区共有四十家米店和一家米行。前者的十三家无现货库存，其余各家存有一担至三十四担不等，总计二百四十一担。那一家米行存有五十担。

Recently a consignment of 13 H rice was 
.  peoured by the Ya Chong Tuh Rice Shop ( tt: ) at 
YY No. 206 Avenue Road from merchants' in Wuish. It was 
transported here by the Yung Shing Transportation Company 
y ee et 4é| ). Unexpectedly on the day following the 
rival of this consignment, three officials of the Japanese 
“SY authorities called at the shop and demanded an inspection 
of the transportation permit for this consignment. 
Alleging that the permit was a counterfeit, the 
officials declared that the shop was not allowed to sell the 
rice and attempted to remove the whole consignment. : 


On the ground that the question of transportation 
permit is one that concerns the transportation company but 
has nothing ‘to do with the shop responsible for the disposal 
of the rice, the shop assistants refused to comply with the 
demand of the Japanese. Subsequently, the Police were 
notified whereupon three Chinese constables were detailed 
to the shop for purposes of protection. ‘As the shop is 
situated in the American Defence Sector, American mar .nes 
were likewise despatched to the place for protection 
purposes in co-operation with the Police. : 

The shop has also 75 bags of rice stored in the 
godown of the Shanghai Commercial & Savings Bank. The shop 
has been notified by the Police not to withdraw this stock 
prior to the solution of the trouble and-has been told to ~ 
ring up the Police any time when disputes take place over 
this matter. 

A similar incident recently took place at the 
Yuan Mou Rice Shop ( * ), Now 13, Lane 344, Burkill 
Road, and protection s thérefore likewise been given td 
it by the American marines and the Police.
